60.ar: الصادق (- عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ (قَال: ... رَجُلٌ مِنَ الْیَهُود ... أَتَی عَلِیّاً (فَسَأَلَه ... قَالَ: یَا یَهُودِی ... وَ أَنْتُمْ تَقُولُونَ: إِنَّ أَوَّلَ عَیْنٍ نَبَعَتْ عَلَی وَجْهِ الْأَرْضِ الْعَیْنُ الَّتِی بِبَیْتِ الْمَقْدِسِ. وَ کَذَبْتُمْ، هِیَ عَیْنُ الْحَیَاةِ الَّتِی غَسَلَ فِیهَا یُوشَعُ بْنُ نُونٍ السَّمَکَةَ وَ هِیَ الْعَیْنُ الَّتِی شَرِبَ مِنْهَا الخِضْر وَ لَیْسَ یَشْرَبُ مِنْهَا أَحَدٌ إِلَّا حَیَّ. قَالَ: صَدَقْتَ، وَ اللَّهِ إِنَّهُ لَبِخَطِّ هَارُونَ وَ إِمْلَاءِ مُوسَی (.
60.fa: از امام صادق (علیه السلام) روایت است: مردی از دانشمندان یهود ... نزد امام علی (علیه السلام) آمد و از ایشان سؤال کرد... امام (علیه السلام) فرمود: «ای یهودی! ... شما می‌گویید نخستین چشمه‌ای که بر روی زمین جوشید، چشمه‌ای بود در بیت المقدس و دروغ می‌گویید. آن چشمه‌ی زندگی است که یوشع‌بن‌نون (علیه السلام)، ماهی را در آن شست و آن چشمه‌ای است که خضر (علیه السلام) از آن نوشید و هیچ کس از آن ننوشد، مگر اینکه زنده می‌ماند». گفت: «راست گفتی! به خدا که این سخن به خط هارون و به املای موسی (علیها السلام) است».
60.en: It is narrated from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him): A man from the Jews came to Imam Ali (peace be upon him) and asked him... The Imam (peace be upon him) said: "O Jew! ... You say that the first spring that gushed forth on the face of the earth was the spring in Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), but you have lied. It is the Spring of Life in which Joshua, son of Nun (peace be upon him), washed the fish, and it is the spring from which al-Khidr (peace be upon him) drank; no one drinks from it but that they remain alive." He said: "You have spoken the truth! By God, this is written in the handwriting of Aaron and dictated by Moses (peace be upon them)."
60.book: Tafsir Ahl al-Bayt (peace be upon them), Vol. 8, p. 522

60.ar: الباقر (- فِی رِوَایَةِ أَبِی الْجَارُود عَنْ أَبِی جَعْفَرٍ (فِی قَوْلِهِ وَ إِذْ قالَ مُوسَی لِفَتاهُ وَ هُوَ یوشع بن نون (وَ قَوْلُهُ لا أَبْرَحُ یَقُولُ لَا أَزَالُ حَتَّی أَبْلُغَ مَجْمَعَ الْبَحْرَیْنِ أَوْ أَمْضِیَ حُقُباً وَ الْحُقُبُ ثَمَانُونَ سَنَةً.
60.fa: در روایت ابوالجارود آمده است: امام باقر (علیه السلام) در مورد آیه: وَ إِذْ قالَ موسی لِفَتاهُ فرمود: مراد از «فتی» یوشع‌بن‌نون (علیه السلام) است و لا أَبْرَحُ یعنی پیوسته حرکت می‌کنم. حَتَّی أَبْلُغَ مَجْمَعَ الْبَحْرَیْنِ أَوْ أَمْضِیَ حُقُباً تا به مجمع البحرین برسم. فرمود: «حقب هشتاد سال است».
60.en: In the narration of Abu al-Jarud, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) said regarding the verse: "And when Moses said to his servant," that the "servant" (fata) refers to Joshua son of Nun (peace be upon him). Regarding the words "I will not cease" (la abrahu), he said: "I will continue to travel until I reach the junction of the two seas, or I will continue for a long period (huqub)." He said: "A huqub is eighty years."
60.book: Tafsir Ahl al-Bayt (peace be upon them), Vol. 8, p. 522
60.refs: Bihar al-Anwar, Vol. 13, p. 286; Al-Qummi, Vol. 2, p. 40; Al-Burhan

60.ar: الرّسول (- لَمَّا أَخْبَرَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ (قُرَیْشاً بِخَبَرِ أَصْحَابِ الْکَهْفِ قَالُوا أَخْبِرْنَا عَنِ الْعَالِمِ الَّذِی أَمَرَ اللَّهُ مُوسَی (أَنْ یَتْبَعَهُ وَ مَا قِصَّتُهُ فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ وَ إِذْ قالَ مُوسَی لِفَتاهُ لا أَبْرَحُ حَتَّی أَبْلُغَ مَجْمَعَ الْبَحْرَیْنِ أَوْ أَمْضِیَ حُقُباً قَالَ وَ کَانَ سَبَبُ ذَلِکَ أَنَّهُ لَمَّا کَلَّمَ اللهُ مُوسَی تَکْلِیماً وَ أَنْزَلَ اللهُ عَلَیْهِ الْأَلْوَاحَ وَ فِیهَا کَمَا قَالَ اللَّهُ وَ کَتَبْنا لَهُ فِی الْأَلْواحِ مِنْ کُلِّ شَیْءٍ مَوْعِظَةً وَ تَفْصِیلًا لِکُلِّ شَیْءٍ وَ رَجَعَ مُوسَی (إِلَی بَنِی إِسْرَائِیلَ فَصَعِدَ الْمِنْبَرَ فَأَخْبَرَهُمْ أَنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ أَنْزَلَ عَلَیْهِ التَّوْرَاةَ وَ کَلَّمَهُ قَالَ فِی نَفْسِهِ مَا خَلَقَ اللَّهُ خَلْقاً أَعْلَمَ مِنِّی فَأَوْحَی اللَّهُ إِلَی جَبْرَئِیلَ (أَدْرِکْ مُوسَی (فَقَدْ هَلَکَ وَ أَعْلِمْهُ أَنَّ عِنْدَ مُلْتَقَی الْبَحْرَیْنِ عِنْدَ الصَّخْرَةِ رَجُلًا أَعْلَمَ مِنْکَ فَصِرْ إِلَیْهِ وَ تَعَلَّمْ مِنْ عِلْمِهِ فَنَزَلَ جَبْرَئِیلَ علَی مُوسَی (وَ أَخْبَرَهُ فَذَلَّ مُوسَی (فِی نَفْسِهِ وَ عَلِمَ أَنَّهُ أَخْطَأَ وَ دَخَلَهُ الرُّعْبُ وَ قَالَ لِوَصِیِّهِ یُوشَعَ (إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ أَمَرَنِی أَنْ أَتَّبِعَ رَجُلًا عِنْدَ مُلْتَقَی الْبَحْرَیْنِ وَ أَتَعَلَّمَ مِنْهُ فَتَزَوَّدَ یُوشَعُ (حُوتاً مَمْلُوحاً وَ خَرَجَا فَلَمَّا خَرَجَا وَ بَلَغَا ذَلِکَ الْمَکَانَ وَجَدَا رَجُلًا مُسْتَلْقِیا علی (قَفَاهُ فَلَمْ یَعْرِفَاهُ فَأَخْرَجَ وَصِیُّ مُوسَی (الْحُوتَ وَ غَسَلَهُ بِالْمَاءِ وَ وَضَعَهُ عَلَی الصَّخْرَةِ وَ مَضَیَا وَ نَسِیَا الْحُوتَ وَ کَانَ ذَلِکَ الْمَاءُ مَاءَ الْحَیَوَانِ فَحَیِیَ الْحُوتُ وَ دَخَلَ فِی الْمَاءِ فَمَضَی مُوسَی (وَ یُوشَعُ (مَعَهُ حَتَّی عَیِیَا فَقَالَ لِوَصِیِّهِ آتِنا غَداءَنا لَقَدْ لَقِینا مِنْ سَفَرِنا هذا نَصَباً أَیْ عَنَاءً فَذَکَرَ وَصِیُّهُ السَّمَکَةَ فَقَالَ لِموسی (إِنِّی نَسِیتُ الْحُوتَ عَلَی الصَّخْرَةِ فَقَالَ مُوسَی (ذَلِکَ الرَّجُلُ الَّذِی رَأَیْنَاهُ عِنْدَ الصَّخْرَةِ هُوَ الَّذِی نُرِیدُهُ فَرَجَعَا عَلی آثارِهِما قَصَصاً إِلَی عِنْدِ الرَّجُلِ وَ هُوَ فِی الصَّلَاةِ فَقَعَدَ مُوسَی (حَتَّی فَرَغَ عَنِ الصَّلَاةِ فَسَلَّمَ عَلَیْهِمَا فَحَدَّثَنِی مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِیِّ بْنِ بِلَالٍ عَنْ یُونُسَ قَالَ اخْتَلَفَ یُونُسُ وَ هِشَامُ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِیمَ فِی الْعَالِمِ الَّذِی أَتَاهُ مُوسَی (أَیُّهُمَا کَانَ أَعْلَمَ وَ هَلْ یَجُوزُ أَنْ یَکُونَ عَلَی مُوسَی (حُجَّةٌ فِی وَقْتِهِ وَ هُوَ حُجَّةُ اللَّهِ عَلَی خَلْقِهِ فَقَالَ قَاسِمٌ الصَّیْقَلُ فَکَتَبُوا إِلَی أَبِی الْحَسَنِ (الرِّضَا (یَسْأَلُونَهُ عَنْ ذَلِکَ فَکَتَبَ فِی الْجَوَابِ أَتَی مُوسَی (الْعَالِمَ فَأَصَابَهُ فِی جَزِیرَةٍ مِنْ جَزَائِرِ الْبَحْرِ إِمَّا جَالِساً وَ إِمَّا مُتَّکِئاً فَسَلَّمَ عَلَیْهِ مُوسَی (فَأَنْکَرَ السَّلَامَ إِذْ کَانَ بِأَرْضٍ لَیْسَ بِهَا سَلَامٌ فَقَالَ مَنْ أَنْتَ قَالَ أَنَا مُوسَی بن عمران (قَالَ أَنْتَ مُوسَی بن عِمْران (الَّذِی کَلَّمَهُ اللهُ تَکْلِیماً قَالَ نَعَمْ قَالَ فَمَا حَاجَتُکَ قَالَ جِئْتُ لِتُعَلِّمَنِی مِمَّا عُلِّمْتَ رُشْداً قَالَ إِنِّی وُکِّلْتُ بِأَمْرٍ لَا تُطِیقُهُ وَ وُکِّلْتَ بِأَمْرِ لَا أُطِیقُهُ ثُمَّ حَدَّثَهُ الْعَالِمُ بِمَا یُصِیبُ آل محمد (مِنَ الْبَلَاءِ حَتَّی اشْتَدَّ بُکَاؤُهُمَا ثُمَّ حَدَّثَهُ عَنْ فَضْلِ آل محمد (حَتَّی جَعَلَ مُوسَی (یَقُولُ یَا لَیْتَنِی کُنْتُ مِنْ آل محمد (وَ حَتَّی ذَکَرَ فُلَاناً وَ فُلَاناً وَ مَبْعَثَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ (إِلَی قَوْمِهِ وَ مَا یَلْقَی مِنْهُمْ وَ مِنْ تَکْذِیبِهِمْ إِیَّاهُ وَ ذَکَرَ لَهُ تَأْوِیلَ هَذِهِ الْآیَةِ وَ نُقَلِّبُ أَفْئِدَتَهُمْ وَ أَبْصارَهُمْ کَما لَمْ یُؤْمِنُوا بِهِ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ حِینَ أُخِذَ الْمِیثَاقُ عَلَیْهِمْ فَقَالَ مُوسَی (هَلْ أَتَّبِعُکَ عَلی أَنْ تُعَلِّمَنِ مِمَّا عُلِّمْتَ رُشْداً فَقَالَ الخِضْر (إِنَّکَ لَنْ تَسْتَطِیعَ مَعِیَ صَبْراً وَ کَیْفَ تَصْبِرُ عَلی ما لَمْ تُحِطْ بِهِ خُبْراً فَقَالَ مُوسَی (سَتَجِدُنِی إِنْ شاءَ اللهُ صابِراً وَ لا أَعْصِی لَکَ أَمْراً قَالَ الخِضْر (فَإِنِ اتَّبَعْتَنِی فَلا تَسْئَلْنِی عَنْ شَیْءٍ حَتَّی أُحْدِثَ لَکَ مِنْهُ ذِکْراً یَقُولُ لَا تَسْأَلْنِی عَنْ شَیْءٍ أَفْعَلُهُ وَ لَا تُنْکِرْهُ عَلَیَّ حَتَّی أُخْبِرَکَ أَنَا بِخَبَرِهِ قَالَ نَعَمْ فَمَرُّوا ثَلَاثَتُهُمْ حَتَّی انْتَهَوْا إِلَی سَاحِلِ الْبَحْرِ وَ قَدْ شُحِنَتْ سَفِینَةٌ وَ هِیَ تُرِیدُ أَنْ تَعْبُرَ فَقَالَ أَرْبَابُ السَّفِینَةِ نَحْمِلُ هَؤُلَاءِ الثَّلَاثَةَ نَفَرٍ فَإِنَّهُمْ قَوْمٌ صَالِحُونَ فَحَمَلُوهُمْ فَلَمَّا جَنَحَتِ السَّفِینَةُ فِی الْبَحْرِ قَامَ الخِضْر (إِلَی جَوَانِبِ السَّفِینَةِ فَکَسَرَهَا وَ حَشَاهَا بِالْخِرَقِ وَ الطِّینِ فَغَضِبَ مُوسَی (غَضَباً شَدِیداً وَ قَالَ لِلْخَضِرِ (أَخَرَقْتَها لِتُغْرِقَ أَهْلَها لَقَدْ جِئْتَ شَیْئاً إِمْراً فَقَالَ لَهُ الخِضْر (أَ لَمْ أَقُلْ إِنَّکَ لَنْ تَسْتَطِیعَ مَعِیَ صَبْراً قَالَ مُوسَی (لا تُؤاخِذْنِی بِما نَسِیتُ وَ لا تُرْهِقْنِی مِنْ أَمْرِی عُسْراً فَخَرَجُوا مِنَ السَّفِینَةِ فَنَظَرَ الخِضْر (إِلَی غُلَامٍ یَلْعَبُ بَیْنَ الصِّبْیَانِ حَسَنِ الْوَجْهِ کَأَنَّهُ قِطْعَةُ قَمَرٍ وَ فِی أُذُنَیْهِ دُرَّتَانِ فَتَأَمَّلَهُ الخِضْر (ثُمَّ أَخَذَهُ وَ قَتَلَهُ فَوَثَبَ مُوسَی (إِلَی الخِضْر (وَ جَلَدَ بِهِ الْأَرْضَ فَقَالَ أَ قَتَلْتَ نَفْساً زَکِیَّةً بِغَیْرِ نَفْسٍ لَقَدْ جِئْتَ شَیْئاً نُکْراً فَقَالَ الخِضْر (لَهُ أَ لَمْ أَقُلْ لَکَ إِنَّکَ لَنْ تَسْتَطِیعَ مَعِیَ صَبْراً قَالَ مُوسَی (إِنْ سَأَلْتُکَ عَنْ شَیْءٍ بَعْدَها فَلا تُصاحِبْنِی قَدْ بَلَغْتَ مِنْ لَدُنِّی عُذْراً فَانْطَلَقا حَتَّی إِذا أَتَیا بِالْعَشِیِّ قَرْیَةً تُسَمَّی النَّاصِرَةَ وَ إِلَیْهَا تُنْسَبُ النَّصَارَی وَ لَمْ یُضَیِّفُوا أَحَداً قَطُّ وَ لَمْ یَطْعَمُوا غَرِیباً فَاسْتَطْعَمُوهُمْ فَلَمْ یُطْعِمُوهُمْ وَ لَمْ یُضَیِّفُوهُمْ فَنَظَرَ الخِضْر (إِلَی حَائِطٍ قَدْ زَالَ لِیَنْهَدِمَ فَوَضَعَ الخِضْر (یَدَهُ عَلَیْهِ وَ قَالَ قُمْ بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ فَقَامَ فَقَالَ مُوسَی (لَمْ یَنْبَغِ أَنْ تُقِیمَ الْجِدَارَ حَتَّی یُطْعِمُونَا وَ یُؤْوُونَا وَ هُوَ قَوْلُهُ لَوْ شِئْتَ لَاتَّخَذْتَ عَلَیْهِ أَجْراً فَقَالَ لَهُ الخِضْر (هذا فِراقُ بَیْنِی وَ بَیْنِکَ سَأُنَبِّئُکَ بِتَأْوِیلِ ما لَمْ تَسْتَطِعْ عَلَیْهِ صَبْراً أَمَّا السَّفِینَةُ الَّتِی فَعَلْتُ بِهَا مَا فَعَلْتُ فَکانَتْ لِقَوْمٍ لِمَساکِینَ یَعْمَلُونَ فِی الْبَحْرِ فَأَرَدْتُ أَنْ أَعِیبَها وَ کَانَ وَرَاءَ السَّفِینَةِ مَلِکٌ یَأْخُذُ کُلَّ سَفِینَةٍ صَالِحَةٍ غَصْباً کَذَا نَزَلَتْ وَ إِذَا کَانَتِ السَّفِینَةُ مَعْیُوبَةً لَمْ یَأْخُذْ مِنْهَا شَیْئاً وَ أَمَّا الْغُلامُ فَکانَ أَبَواهُ مُؤْمِنَیْنِ وَ طُبِعَ کَافِراً کَذَا نَزَلَتْ فَنَظَرْتُ إِلَی جَبِینِهِ وَ عَلَیْهِ مَکْتُوبٌ طُبِعَ کَافِراً فَخَشِینا أَنْ یُرْهِقَهُما طُغْیاناً وَ کُفْراً فَأَرَدْنا أَنْ یُبْدِلَهُما رَبُّهُما خَیْراً مِنْهُ زَکاةً وَ أَقْرَبَ رُحْماً فَأَبْدَلَ اللَّهُ وَالِدَیْهِ بِنْتاً وَلَدَتْ سَبْعِینَ نبیا (وَ أَمَّا الْجِدارُ الَّذِی أَقَمْتُهُ فَکانَ لِغُلامَیْنِ یَتِیمَیْنِ فِی الْمَدِینَةِ وَ کانَ تَحْتَهُ کَنْزٌ لَهُما وَ کانَ أَبُوهُما صالِحاً فَأَرادَ رَبُّکَ أَنْ یَبْلُغا أَشُدَّهُما إِلَی قَوْلِهِ ذلِکَ تَأْوِیلُ ما لَمْ تَسْطِعْ عَلَیْهِ صَبْراً.
60.en:
When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) informed the Quraysh of the story of the Companions of the Cave, they said, "Tell us about the scholar whom Allah commanded Moses (peace be upon him) to follow, and what his story was." So Allah, the Almighty and Majestic, revealed: "And [mention] when Moses said to his servant, 'I will not cease until I reach the junction of the two seas or continue for a long period.'" (18:60).

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: "The reason for this was that when Allah spoke to Moses directly and sent down the Tablets upon him—containing what Allah described: 'And We wrote for him on the tablets [something] of all things—instruction and explanation for all things' (7:145)—Moses (peace be upon him) returned to the Children of Israel. He ascended the pulpit and informed them that Allah had sent down the Torah to him and had spoken to him. He said to himself, 'Allah has not created any creature more learned than me.'

Thereupon, Allah revealed to Gabriel: 'Overtake Moses, for he has perished, and inform him that at the junction of the two seas, by the rock, there is a man more learned than you. Go to him and learn from his knowledge.' Gabriel descended to Moses (peace be upon him) and informed him. Moses (peace be upon him) felt humbled within himself, realized he had erred, and was seized with fear. He said to his successor, Joshua (peace be upon him), 'Allah has commanded me to follow a man at the junction of the two seas and to learn from him.' Joshua (peace be upon him) took a salted fish as provisions, and they set out.

When they reached that place, they found a man lying on his back. They did not recognize him. Moses’ successor (peace be upon him) took out the fish, washed it with water, and placed it on the rock. They continued on their way and forgot the fish. That water was the Water of Life; the fish came to life and entered the water. Moses (peace be upon him) and Joshua (peace be upon him) continued until they became exhausted. He said to his successor, 'Bring us our morning meal. We have certainly suffered much fatigue from this journey.' His successor remembered the fish and said to Moses (peace be upon him), 'I forgot the fish at the rock.' Moses (peace be upon him) said, 'That man we saw at the rock is the one we are seeking.' They returned, retracing their footsteps, until they reached the man, who was in prayer. Moses (peace be upon him) sat until he finished his prayer, and then he greeted them.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Bilal narrated to me from Yunus, who said: Yunus and Hisham ibn Ibrahim differed regarding the scholar whom Moses (peace be upon him) visited—which of them was more learned, and is it permissible for there to be a proof (hujjah) over Moses (peace be upon him) in his time, while he is Allah’s proof over His creation? Qasim al-Sayqal said: They wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) asking him about this. He wrote in his reply: 'Moses (peace be upon him) came to the scholar and found him on one of the islands of the sea, either sitting or reclining. Moses (peace be upon him) greeted him, but he did not return the greeting, as he was in a land where there was no greeting. He asked, "Who are you?" He replied, "I am Moses son of Imran." He asked, "Are you the Moses son of Imran to whom Allah spoke directly?" He said, "Yes." He asked, "What is your need?" He said, "I have come so that you may teach me of what you have been taught of guidance." He said, "I have been entrusted with a matter you cannot bear, and you have been entrusted with a matter I cannot bear."

Then the scholar told him of the calamities that would befall the Family of Muhammad (peace be upon them), until they both wept intensely. Then he told him of the excellence of the Family of Muhammad (peace be upon them), until Moses (peace be upon him) began to say, "Would that I were of the Family of Muhammad!" He even mentioned so-and-so and so-and-so, and the mission of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) to his people, and what he would encounter from them and their denial of him. He mentioned to him the interpretation of this verse: "And We will turn away their hearts and their eyes just as they refused to believe in it the first time, when the covenant was taken from them" (6:110).

Moses (peace be upon him) said, "May I follow you on [the condition] that you teach me from what you have been taught of guidance?" Al-Khidr (peace be upon him) said, "Indeed, with me you will never be able to have patience. And how can you have patience for what you do not encompass in knowledge?" Moses (peace be upon him) said, "You will find me, if Allah wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any order." Al-Khidr (peace be upon him) said, "If you follow me, then do not ask me about anything until I make mention of it to you." He meant: Do not ask me about anything I do, and do not object to it, until I inform you of its explanation. He said, "Yes."

The three of them passed by until they reached the seashore, where a ship was loaded and ready to cross. The owners of the ship said, "We will carry these three men, for they are righteous people." They carried them. When the ship leaned into the sea, Al-Khidr (peace be upon him) stood up to the sides of the ship, broke them, and stuffed them with rags and mud. Moses (peace be upon him) became intensely angry and said to Al-Khidr (peace be upon him), "Have you torn it to drown its people? You have certainly done a grave thing." Al-Khidr (peace be upon him) said to him, "Did I not say that you would never be able to have patience with me?" Moses (peace be upon him) said, "Do not blame me for what I forgot and do not constrain me in my matter with difficulty."

They exited the ship. Al-Khidr (peace be upon him) looked at a boy playing among the children, beautiful of face as if he were a piece of the moon, with two pearls in his ears. Al-Khidr (peace be upon him) contemplated him, then took him and killed him. Moses (peace be upon him) sprang at Al-Khidr (peace be upon him) and threw him to the ground, saying, "Have you killed a pure soul for other than [having killed] a soul? You have certainly done a deplorable thing." Al-Khidr (peace be upon him) said to him, "Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me?" Moses (peace be upon him) said, "If I should ask you about anything after this, then do not keep me as a companion. You have already obtained from me an excuse."

They departed until, in the evening, they came to a village called Nasirah—to which the Christians are attributed—and they had never hosted anyone nor fed a stranger. They asked them for food, but they did not feed them nor host them. Al-Khidr (peace be upon him) looked at a wall that was about to collapse, so he placed his hand upon it and said, "Stand by the permission of Allah," and it stood. Moses (peace be upon him) said, "It was not appropriate to set up the wall until they fed us and sheltered us," which is his saying: "If you had wished, you could have taken for it a payment."

Al-Khidr (peace be upon him) said to him, "This is the parting between me and you. I will inform you of the interpretation of that about which you could not have patience. As for the ship, I did what I did because it belonged to poor people working at sea, and I wanted to cause a defect in it, for behind the ship was a king who seized every sound ship by force—that is how it was revealed—and if the ship was defective, he would not take anything from it. As for the boy, his parents were believers, and he was created a disbeliever—that is how it was revealed—so I looked at his forehead and upon it was written "created a disbeliever," and we feared that he would burden them with tyranny and disbelief. So we wanted their Lord to replace him with one better than him in purity and closer in mercy. Allah replaced their parents with a daughter who gave birth to seventy prophets (peace be upon them). As for the wall I set up, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and beneath it was a treasure for them, and their father was a righteous man. So your Lord intended that they reach their maturity—up to his saying—that is the interpretation of that about which you could not have patience.'"
60.book: Tafsir Ahl al-Bayt (peace be upon them), Vol. 8, p. 522
60.refs: Bihar al-Anwar, Vol. 13, p. 278; Al-Qummi, Vol. 2, p. 37; Nur al-Thaqalayn (with variation); Al-Burhan.

مُوسَی (یَقْتَصُّ أَثَرَهُ حَتَّی انْتَهَی إِلَیْهِ وَ هُوَ عَلَی حَالِهِ مُسْتَلْقٍ فَقَالَ لَهُ مُوسَی (السَّلَامُ عَلَیْکَ فَقَالَ وَ عَلَیْکَ السَّلَامُ یَا عَالِمَ بَنِی إِسْرَائِیل قَالَ ثُمَّ نَسِیتُ وَ لا تُرْهِقْنِی مِنْ أَمْرِی عُسْراً قَالَ وَ خَرَجَا عَلَی سَاحِلِ الْبَحْرِ فَإِذَا غُلَامٌ یَلْعَبُ مَعَ غِلْمَانٍ عَلَیْهِ قَمِیصُ حَرِیرٍ أَخْضَرُ فِی أُذُنَیْهِ دُرَّتَانِ 60.en: Abd al-Rahman ibn Siyabah narrates: Imam al-Sadiq (as) said: "Moses (as) ascended the pulpit, and his pulpit had three steps. He thought to himself that God had not created any creature more knowledgeable than him. Gabriel (as) came to him and said: 'You have been tested; descend, for there is someone on earth who is more knowledgeable than you. Seek him out.' Moses (as) sent for Joshua (as) and said: 'I have been tested, so prepare provisions and come with me.' Joshua (as) bought a fish, went to Azerbaijan, roasted it, and placed it in a basket. Then they set out together until they reached the seashore... They walked until they reached an old man lying down, with his staff placed beside him and a cloak over him. It was not long enough for his stature; if he covered his head, his feet would be exposed, and if he covered his feet, his head would be exposed. Moses (as) stood to pray and said to Joshua (as): 'Watch over me.' A drop of rain fell from the sky into the basket. The fish stirred and began dragging the basket toward the sea. This is the meaning of His saying: '...and it took its course into the sea, disappearing' (18:61). Then a bird descended, landed on the seashore, and dipped its beak into the water. It said to Moses (as): 'O Moses (as)! You have not taken from the knowledge of your Lord except what the back of my beak has gathered from the entire sea.' Then Moses (as) stood up and walked, and Joshua (as) followed him. After a long time, Moses (as) became tired and said to Joshua (as): 'When they had passed beyond [that place], [Moses] said to his servant: Bring us our morning meal; we have indeed suffered much fatigue in this journey of ours' (18:62) ... '...and it took its course into the sea, in a wondrous way' (18:63). Moses (as) returned, tracing his steps until he reached him, and he was still in the same state, lying down. Moses (as) said to him: 'Peace be upon you.' He replied: 'And upon you be peace, O scholar of the Children of Israel.' Then he jumped up and took his staff in his hand. Moses (as) said to him: 'I have been commanded to follow you so that you may teach me from what you have been taught of guidance.' He replied, as has been narrated to you: 'You will never be able to bear with me patiently' (18:67). They set out until they reached a ferry. When the people of the ferry saw them, they said: 'By God, we will not take any payment from these people today; we will carry them.' When the boat reached the middle of the water, he [the scholar] breached it. Moses (as) said to him as you have been told, then he said: 'Did I not say that you would never be able to bear with me patiently?' [Moses] said: 'Do not punish me for what I forgot, and do not impose upon me difficulty in my affair' (18:73). They went out onto the seashore and found a boy playing with other boys, wearing a shirt of green silk with two pearls in his ears. The scholar overpowered him and slaughtered him. Moses (as) said to him: 'Have you killed a pure soul without [the killing of] a soul? You have indeed done a terrible thing!' (18:74). They continued until they came to the people of a village; they asked its people for food, but they refused to host them. Then they found therein a wall that was about to collapse, and [the scholar] set it upright. [Moses] said: 'If you had wished, you could have taken payment for it' (18:77), meaning: 'If only you had taken bread so that we could eat, for we have become hungry.' This is a village on the seashore called Nasirah, and the Christians (Nasara) are named after it. They did not host them, and they will not host anyone after them until the Hour is established. The parable of the boat among you and us is the refusal of al-Husayn (as) to pledge allegiance to Mu'awiyah. The parable of the boy among you is the statement of al-Hasan ibn Ali (as) to Abdullah ibn Ali: 'May God curse you, for you are an evil disbeliever.' It was said to him: 'O Abu Muhammad (as)! You have killed him.' And the parable of the wall among you is Ali (as), al-Hasan (as), and al-Husayn (as)."
60.refs: Bihar al-Anwar, Vol. 13, p. 306; al-Ayyashi, Vol. 2, p. 332; Nur al-Thaqalayn; "with slight differences in wording"; al-Burhan

60.ar: الصّادقین (- عَنْ زُرَارَةَ وَ حُمْرَانَ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِی جَعْفَرٍ وَ أَبِی عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (قَالَ: إِنَّهُ لَمَّا کَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ مُوسَی (الَّذِی کَانَ أُعْطِیَ مکتل {مِکْتَلًا} فِیهِ حُوتٌ مُمَلَّحٌ وَ قِیلَ لَهُ: هَذَا یَدُلُّکَ عَلَی صَاحِبِکَ عِنْدَ عَیْنِ مَجْمَعِ الْبَحْرَیْنِ لَا یُصِیبُ مِنْهَا شَیْءٌ مَیِّتاً إِلَّا حَیِیَ، یُقَالُ لَهُ: الْحَیَاةُ، فَانْطَلَقَا حَتَّی بَلَغَا الصَّخْرَةَ فَانْطَلَقَ الْفَتَی یَغْسِلُ الْحُوتَ فِی الْعَیْنِ فَاضْطَرَبَ فِی یَدِهِ حَتَّی خَدَشَهُ وَ انْفَلَتَ مِنْهُ وَ نَسِیَهُ الْفَتَی. فَلَمَّا جَاوَزَ الْوَقْتَ الَّذِی وُقِّتَ فِیهِ أَعْیَا مُوسَی وَ قَالَ لِفَتَاهُ: آتِنا غَداءَنا لَقَدْ لَقِینا مِنْ سَفَرِنا هذا نَصَباً قالَ أَ رَأَیْتَ إِلَی قَوْلِهِ عَلی آثارِهِما قَصَصاً. فَلَمَّا أَتَاهَا وَجَدَ الْحُوتَ قَدْ خَرَّ فِی الْبَحْرِ فَاقْتَصَّا الْأَثَرَ حَتَّی أَتَیَا صَاحِبَهُمَا فِی جَزِیرَةٍ مِنْ جَزَائِرِ الْبَحْرِ إِمَّا مُتَّکِئاً وَ إِمَّا جَالِساً فِی کِسَاءٍ لَهُ فَسَلَّمَ عَلَیْهِ مُوسَی فَعَجِبَ مِنَ السَّلَامِ وَ هُوَ فِی أَرْضٍ لَیْسَ فِیهَا السَّلَامُ فَقَالَ: مَنْ أَنْتَ؟ قَالَ: أَنَا مُوسَی. قَالَ: أَنْتَ مُوسَی بْنُ عِمْرَانَ الَّذِی کَلَّمَهُ اللَّهُ تَکْلِیماً؟ قَالَ: نَعَمْ. قَالَ: فَمَا حَاجَتُکَ؟ قَالَ: أَتَّبِعُکَ عَلی أَنْ تُعَلِّمَنِ مِمَّا عُلِّمْتَ رُشْداً. قَالَ: إِنِّی وُکِّلْتُ بِأَمْرٍ لَا تُطِیقُهُ وَ وُکِّلْتَ بِأَمْرٍ لَا أُطِیقُهُ. وَ قَدْ قَالَ لَهُ: إِنَّکَ لَنْ تَسْتَطِیعَ مَعِیَ صَبْراً وَ کَیْفَ تَصْبِرُ عَلی ما لَمْ تُحِطْ بِهِ خُبْراً قالَ سَتَجِدُنِی إِنْ شاءَ اللهُ صابِراً وَ لا أَعْصِی لَکَ أَمْراً فَحَدَّثَهُ عَنْ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ عَمَّا یُصِیبُهُمْ حَتَّی اشْتَدَّ بُکَاؤُهُمَا ثُمَّ حَدَّثَهُ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ (وَ عَنْ أَمِیرِ الْمُؤْمِنِینَ (وَ عَنْ وُلْدِ فَاطِمَةَ وَ ذَکَرَ لَهُ مِنْ فَضْلِهِمْ وَ مَا أُعْطُوا حَتَّی جَعَلَ یَقُولُ یَا لَیْتَنِی مِنْ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ عَنْ رُجُوعِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ (إِلَی قَوْمِهِ وَ مَا یَلْقَی مِنْهُمْ وَ مِنْ تَکْذِیبِهِمْ إِیَّاهُ وَ تَلَا هَذِهِ الْآیَةَ وَ نُقَلِّبُ أَفْئِدَتَهُمْ وَ أَبْصارَهُمْ کَما لَمْ یُؤْمِنُوا بِهِ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ فَإِنَّهُ أَخَذَ عَلَیْهِمُ الْمِیثَاقَ.
60.en: Zurarah, Humran, and Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Imam al-Baqir and Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon them): When the matter of Musa (peace be upon him) occurred, he was given a basket containing a salted fish, and it was said to him: "This will guide you to your companion at the spring of the junction of the two seas. Nothing dead touches that water but it comes to life; it is called the Water of Life." They set out until they reached the rock. The young man went to wash the fish in the spring, and it thrashed in his hand until it scratched him and escaped, and the young man forgot it. When they passed the appointed time, Musa became weary and said to his young companion: "Bring us our morning meal; indeed, we have suffered much fatigue from this journey of ours." He said: "Did you see [what happened] when we took refuge at the rock? Indeed, I forgot the fish, and none made me forget it except Satan, that I should mention it. And it took its course into the sea, amazingly." He said: "That is what we were seeking." So they returned, tracing their footsteps. When they reached it, he found the fish had fallen into the sea. They followed their tracks until they came to their companion on one of the islands of the sea, either reclining or sitting on a cloak of his. Musa greeted him, and he was surprised by the greeting, as he was in a land where there was no greeting. He asked: "Who are you?" He replied: "I am Musa." He asked: "Are you Musa ibn Imran, to whom Allah spoke directly?" He said: "Yes." He asked: "What is your need?" He said: "May I follow you on [the condition] that you teach me from what you have been taught of sound judgment?" He said: "I have been entrusted with a matter you cannot bear, and you have been entrusted with a matter I cannot bear." And he had said to him: "Indeed, you will never be able to have patience with me. And how can you have patience for what you do not encompass in knowledge?" He said: "You will find me, if Allah wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any order." Then he spoke to him about the Family of Muhammad and what would befall them, until they both wept intensely. Then he spoke to him about the Messenger of Allah, the Commander of the Faithful, and the descendants of Fatima, and mentioned their excellence and what they had been granted, until Musa began to say: "I wish I were of the Family of Muhammad." He also spoke of the return of the Messenger of Allah to his people and what he would encounter from them and their denial of him, and he recited this verse: "And We will turn their hearts and their eyes just as they refused to believe in it the first time," for He had taken the covenant from them.
60.book: Tafsir Ahl al-Bayt (peace be upon them), Vol. 8, p. 530

60.ar: ابن عبّاس (- إِنَّ مُوسَی (لَمَّا أَحْکَمَ التَّوْرَاةَ وَ عَلِمَ مَا فِیهَا، قَالَ فِی نَفْسِهِ: لَمْ یَبْقَ فِی الْأَرْضِ أَحَدٌ أَعْلَمُ مِنِّی مِنْ غَیْرِ أَنْ یَتَکَلَّمَ مَعَ أَحَدٍ. فَرَأَی فِی مَنَامِهِ کَانَ اللَّهُ أَرْسَلَ الْمَاءَ بِالْمَاءِ حَتَّی غَرِقَ مَا بَیْنَ الْمَشْرِقِ وَ الْمَغْرِبِ فَرَأَی فَتَاهُ عَلَی الْبَحْرِ فِیهَا صَرِدَةٌ فَکَانَتِ الصَّرِدَةُ تَجِیءُ لِلْمَاءِ الَّذِی غَرِقَ الْأَرْضَ فَتَنْقُلُ الْمَاءَ بِمِنْقَارِهَا ثُمَّ تَدْفَعُهُ فِی الْبَحْرِ. فَلَمَّا اسْتَیْقَظَ الْکَلِیمُ هَالَهُ ذَلِکَ فَجَاءَهُ جَبْرَائِیلُ (فَقَالَ: مَا لِی أَرَاکَ یَا مُوسَی (کَئِیباً؟ فَأَخْبَرَهُ بِالرُّؤْیَا، فَقَالَ: إِنَّکَ زَعَمْتَ أَنَّکَ اسْتَغْرَقْتَ الْعِلْمَ کُلَّهُ فَلَمْ یَبْقَ فِی الْأَرْضِ مَنْ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ مِنْکَ وَ إِنَّ لِلَّهِ عَبْداً عِلْمُکَ فِی عِلْمِهِ کَالْمَاءِ الَّذِی حَمَلَتْهُ الصَّرِدَةُ بِمِنْقَارِهَا فَدَفَعَتْهُ فِی الْبَحْرِ. فَقَالَ: یَا جَبْرَائِیلُ (مَنْ هَذَا الْعَبْدُ؟ فَقَالَ: الخِضْر بْنُ عَامِیلَ مِنْ وُلْدِ الطَّیِّبِ یَعْنِی إِبْرَاهِیمَ الْخَلِیلَ (قَالَ: مِنْ أَیْنَ أَطْلُبُهُ؟ قَالَ: اطْلُبْهُ مِنْ وَرَاءِ هَذَا الْبَحْرِ. فَقَالَ: مَنْ یَدُلُّنِی عَلَیْهِ؟ قَالَ: بَعْضُ زَادِکَ. قَالُوا: فَمِنْ حِرْصِهِ عَلَی رُؤْیَاهُ لَمْ یَسْتَخْلِفْ فِی قَوْمِهِ وَ مَضَی لِوَجْهِهِ، وَ قَالَ لِفَتاهُ یُوشَعَ: هَلْ أَنْتَ مُوَازِرِی؟ قَالَ: نَعَمْ. قَالَ: اذْهَبْ فَاحْتَمِلْ لَنَا زَاداً. فَانْطَلَقَ یُوشَعُ (فَاحْتَمَلَ أَرْغِفَةً وَ سَمَکَةً عَتِیقَةً مَالِحَةً ثُمَّ سَارَا فِی الْبَحْرِ حَتَّی خَاضَا وَحَلاً وَ طِیناً وَ لَقِیَا تَعَباً وَ نَصَباً حَتَّی انْتَهَیَا إِلَی صَخْرَةٍ نَاتِئَةٍ فِی الْبَحْرِ خَلْفَ بَحْرِ أَرْمَنِیَّةٍ {إِرْمِینِیَّةٍ} یُقَالُ لِتِلْکَ الصَّخْرَةِ: قَلْعَةُ الْحَرْسِ.
60.fa: چون موسی (علیه السلام) تورات را خوب آموخت و هرچه در آن است دانست با خود گفت: «در زمین داناتری از من نمانده است» و این را به کسی نگفت، و در خواب دید که خدا آب را بر آب فرستاد تا هرچه میان خاور و باختر بود غرق شد، و دید که بر دریا چیزی است که بر آن یک جغد است که می‌آید آب‌هایی که زمین را غرق کرده با نوکش می‌گیرد و به دریا می‌ریزد». و هنگامی‌که موسی (علیه السلام) بیدار شد به هراس افتاد و جبرئیل آمد، و گفت: «ای موسی (علیه السلام) چرا تو را اندوهگین می‌بینم»؟ و خوابش را به او گفت و به او پاسخ داد که تو می‌پنداری که همه‌ی دانش را غرقه‌ی خود کردی و در زمین داناتر از تو نیست، و خدا بنده‌ی دیگری ندارد که دانشت نسبت به دانش خدا چون آبی است که جغد با نوکش به دریا می‌ریزد، گفت: «ای جبرئیل این بنده‌ی خدا کیست»؟ گفت: «خضربن‌عامیل از فرزندان مردی پاک یعنی ابراهیم خلیل (علیه السلام) گفت: «از کجا او را بجویم»؟ گفت: «از پس این دریا»، گفت: «چه کسی مرا به او راهنمایی نماید»؟ گفت: «برخی از توشه‌ی تو». موسی (علیه السلام) از حرص بر خوابش جانشینی برای خود در قومش معیّن نکرد و به‌دنبال کارش رفت و به جوانش یوشع (علیه السلام) گفت: «آیا تو پشتیبان من هستی»؟ گفت: «آری»، گفت: «پس برو توشه‌ای برای ما بگیر، یوشع (علیه السلام) رفت و چند قرص نان و ماهی شوری کهنه برداشت و در دریا رفتند تا به لجن و گل فرو رفتند و رنج و خستگی فراوان دیدند تا بدان صخره رسیدند که در پشت دریای ارمینیه از دریا برآمده بود و به آن صخره در پاسبانان می‌گفتند. و نزد آن آمدند و موسی (علیه السلام) رفت و وضو گرفت و به جایی وارد شد و یک چشمه‌ی بهشتی در دریا یافت».
60.en: When Moses (peace be upon him) had mastered the Torah and understood all that was within it, he said to himself, "There remains no one on earth more knowledgeable than I," without speaking this to anyone. He then saw in a dream that God had sent water upon water until everything between the East and the West was submerged. He saw upon the sea a creature, and upon it was a bird (a shrike/owl), which would come to the water that had flooded the earth, take the water in its beak, and cast it into the sea. When Moses (peace be upon him) awoke, he was struck with awe. Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to him and said, "O Moses, why do I see you sorrowful?" He told him of the dream. Gabriel replied, "You claimed that you had encompassed all knowledge and that there remained no one on earth more knowledgeable than you, yet God has another servant whose knowledge compared to God's knowledge is like the water that the bird carried in its beak and cast into the sea." Moses asked, "O Gabriel, who is this servant?" He replied, "Al-Khidr ibn Amil, from the descendants of the Pure One, meaning Abraham the Friend (peace be upon him)." Moses asked, "Where shall I seek him?" He said, "Seek him beyond this sea." Moses asked, "Who will guide me to him?" He said, "Some of your provisions." It is said that due to his eagerness regarding his dream, he did not appoint a successor over his people and set out on his journey. He said to his young attendant, Joshua (peace be upon him), "Will you be my supporter?" He replied, "Yes." He said, "Go and take provisions for us." Joshua (peace be upon him) went and took some loaves of bread and a piece of old, salted fish. They traveled across the sea until they waded through mud and mire, and they encountered hardship and fatigue until they reached a protruding rock in the sea, behind the sea of Armenia. That rock is called the Fortress of the Guards.
60.book: Tafsir Ahl al-Bayt (peace be upon them), Vol. 8, p. 532

60.ar: الصّادق (- عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ سَالِمٍ عَنْ أَبِی عَبْدِاللهِ (قَالَ: کَانَ مُوسَی (أَعْلَمَ مِنَ الخِضْر (.
60.fa: موسی (علیه السلام) از خضر (علیه السلام) داناتر بود.
60.en: Hisham ibn Salim narrated from Abu Abd Allah (al-Sadiq) (as) who said: "Moses (as) was more knowledgeable than al-Khidr (as)."

60.ar: الصّادق (- کَانَ سُلَیْمَانُ (أَعْلَمَ مِنْ آصَفَ وَ کَانَ مُوسَی (أَعْلَمَ مِنَ الَّذِی اتَّبَعَهُ.
60.fa: سلیمان (علیه السلام) از آصف داناتر بود و موسی (علیه السلام) از کسی که به دنبالش روان بود (خضر (علیه السلام)) داناتر بود».
60.en: Solomon (as) was more knowledgeable than Asif, and Moses (as) was more knowledgeable than the one he followed (al-Khidr (as)).

60.ar: الباقر (- عَنْ سَیْفٍ التَّمَّارِ قَالَ کُنَّا مَعَ أَبِی عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (جَمَاعَةً مِنَ الشِّیعَةِ فِی الْحِجْرِ فَقَالَ عَلَیْنَا عَیْنٌ فَالْتَفَتْنَا یَمْنَةً وَ یَسْرَةً فَلَمْ نَرَ أَحَداً فَقُلْنَا لَیْسَ عَلَیْنَا عَیْنٌ فَقَالَ وَ رَبِّ الْکَعْبَةِ وَ رَبِّ الْبَنِیَّةِ ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ لَوْ کُنْتُ بَیْنَ مُوسَی وَ الخِضْر لَأَخْبَرْتُهُمَا أَنِّی أَعْلَمُ مِنْهُمَا وَ لَأَنْبَأْتُهُمَا بِمَا لَیْسَ فِی أَیْدِیهِمَا لِأَنَّ مُوسَی وَ الخِضْر أُعْطِیَا عِلْمَ مَا کَانَ وَ لَمْ یُعْطَیَا عِلْمَ مَا یَکُونُ وَ مَا هُوَ کَائِنٌ حَتَّی تَقُومَ السَّاعَةُ وَ قَدْ وَرِثْنَاهُ مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ (وِرَاثَة.
60.fa: سیف تمّار گوید: با گروهی از شیعیان با امام صادق (علیه السلام) در حجر نشسته بودیم که ایشان فرمود: «یک چشم - جاسوس - به ما نگاه می کند»، به راست و چپ خود نگاه کردیم ولی کس--ی را ندیدیم. گفتیم: «کس-ی به ما نگاه نمی‌کند». سه بار فرمود: «قسم به خدای کعبه، قسم به خدای آن خانه، اگر بین موسی و خضر (علیها السلام) بودم به آن‌ها خبر می‌دادم که من از آن‌ها عالم‌تر هستم و به آنچه در دستانشان نبود خبر می‌دادم. چون علم آنچه که اتفاق افتاده به آن‌ها داده شده ولی به آنها علم حوادث آینده و آنچه تا روز قیامت اتفاق می‌افتد داده نشده و ما اهل بیت این علم را از پیامبر (صلی الله علیه و آله) به ارث برده‌ایم».
60.en: Sayf al-Tammar said: We were with Abu Abd Allah (Imam al-Sadiq) along with a group of the Shia in the Hijr, when he said, "There is a spy watching us." We looked to our right and left but did not see anyone. We said, "There is no one watching us." He said, "By the Lord of the Kaaba, by the Lord of the House," three times, "If I were between Moses and al-Khidr, I would inform them that I am more knowledgeable than both of them, and I would inform them of what is not in their possession. For Moses and al-Khidr were given the knowledge of what has been, but they were not given the knowledge of what will be and what is to come until the Hour is established; and we have inherited this from the Messenger of Allah (blessings of Allah be upon him and his family) as an inheritance."
60.book: Tafsir Ahl al-Bayt (peace be upon them), Vol. 8, p. 532
60.refs: Ta'wil al-Ayat al-Zahirah, p. 110; Nur al-Thaqalayn

60.via: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) - narrated by Ishaq ibn Ammar
60.ar: الصّادق (- عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِی عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (قَالَ: إِنَّمَا مَثَلُ عَلِیٍّ (وَ مَثَلُنَا مِنْ بَعْدِهِ مِنْ هَذِهِ الْأُمَّةِ کَمَثَلِ مُوسَی النَّبِیِّ (وَ الْعَالِمِ حِینَ لَقِیَهُ وَ اسْتَنْطَقَهُ وَ سَأَلَهُ الصُّحْبَةَ فَکَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِهِمَا مَا اقْتَصَّهُ اللَّهُ لِنَبِیِّهِ (فِی کِتَابِهِ وَ ذَلِکَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ قَالَ لِمُوسَی إِنِّی اصْطَفَیْتُکَ عَلَی النَّاسِ بِرِسالاتِی وَ بِکَلامِی فَخُذْ ما آتَیْتُکَ وَ کُنْ مِنَ الشَّاکِرِینَ ثُمَّ قَالَ وَ کَتَبْنا لَهُ فِی الْأَلْواحِ مِنْ کُلِّ شَیْءٍ مَوْعِظَةً وَ تَفْصِیلًا لِکُلِّ شَیْءٍ وَ قَدْ کَانَ عِنْدَ الْعَالِمِ عِلْمٌ لَمْ یُکْتَبْ لِمُوسَی فِی الْأَلْوَاحِ وَ کَانَ مُوسَی یَظُنُّ أَنَّ جَمِیعَ الْأَشْیَاءِ الَّتِی یَحْتَاجُ إِلَیْهَا وَ جَمِیعَ الْعِلْمِ قَدْ کُتِبَ لَهُ فِی الْأَلْوَاحِ کَمَا یَظُنُّ هَؤُلَاءِ الَّذِینَ یَدَّعُونَ أَنَّهُمْ فُقَهَاءُ وَ عُلَمَاءُ وَ أَنَّهُمْ قَدْ أَثْبَتُوا جَمِیعَ الْعِلْمِ وَ الْفِقْهِ فِی الدِّینِ مِمَّا یَحْتَاجُ هَذِهِ الْأُمَّةُ إِلَیْهِ وَ صَحَّ لَهُمْ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ (وَ عَلِمُوهُ وَ لَفَظُوهُ وَ لَیْسَ کُلُّ عِلْمِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ (عَلِمُوهُ وَ لَا صَارَ إِلَیْهِمْ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ (وَ لَا عَرَفُوهُ وَ ذَلِکَ أَنَّ الشَّیْءَ مِنَ الْحَلَالِ وَ الْحَرَامِ وَ الْأَحْکَامِ یَرِدُ عَلَیْهِمْ فَیُسْأَلُونَ عَنْهُ وَ لَا یَکُونُ عِنْدَهُمْ فِیهِ أَثَرٌ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ (وَ یَسْتَحْیُونَ أَنْ یَنْسُبَهُمُ النَّاسُ إِلَی الْجَهْلِ وَ یَکْرَهُونَ أَنْ یُسْأَلُوا فَلَا یُجِیبُوا فَیَطْلُبَ النَّاسُ الْعِلْمَ مِنْ مَعْدِنِهِ فَلِذَلِکَ اسْتَعْمَلُوا الرَّأْیَ وَ الْقِیَاسَ فِی دِینِ اللَّهِ وَ تَرَکُوا الْآثَارَ وَ دَانُوا لِلَّهِ بِالْبِدَعِ وَ قَدْ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ (کُلُّ بِدْعَةٍ ضَلَالَةٌ فَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ إِذْ سُئِلُوا عَنْ شَیْءٍ مِن دِینِ اللَّهِ فَلَمْ یَکُنْ عِنْدَهُمْ مِنْهُ أَثَرٌ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ (رَدُّوهُ إِلَی اللَّهِ وَ إِلَی الرَّسُولِ وَ إِلی أُولِی الْأَمْرِ مِنْهُمْ لَعَلِمَهُ الَّذِینَ یَسْتَنْبِطُونَهُ مِنْهُمْ مِنْ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ الَّذِینَ مَنَعَهُمْ مِنْ طَلَبِ الْعِلْمِ مِنَّا الْعَدَاوَةُ وَ الْحَسَدُ لَنَا وَ لَا وَ اللَّهِ مَا حَسَدَ مُوسَی الْعَالِمَ وَ مُوسَی نَبِیُّ اللَّهِ یُوحَی إِلَیْهِ حَیْثُ لَقِیَهُ وَ اسْتَنْطَقَهُ وَ عَرَفَهُ بِالْعِلْمِ وَ لَمْ یَحْسُدْهُ کَمَا حَسَدَتْنَا هَذِهِ الْأُمَّةُ بَعْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ (عِلْمَنَا وَ مَا وَرِثْنَا عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ (وَ لَمْ یَرْغَبُوا إِلَیْنَا فِی عِلْمِنَا کَمَا رَغِبَ مُوسَی إِلَی الْعَالِمِ وَ سَأَلَهُ الصُّحْبَةَ لِیَتَعَلَّمَ مِنْهُ الْعِلْمَ وَ یُرْشِدَهُ فَلَمَّا أَنْ سَأَلَ الْعَالِمَ ذَلِکَ عَلِمَ الْعَالِمُ أَنَّ مُوسَی لَا یَسْتَطِیعُ صُحْبَتَهُ وَ لَا یَحْتَمِلُ عِلْمَهُ وَ لَا یَصْبِرُ مَعَهُ فَعِنْدَ ذَلِکَ قَالَ الْعَالِمُ وَ کَیْفَ تَصْبِرُ عَلی ما لَمْ تُحِطْ بِهِ خُبْراً فَقَالَ لَهُ مُوسَی وَ هُوَ خَاضِعٌ لَهُ یَسْتَنْطِقُهُ عَلَی نَفْسِهِ کَیْ یَقْبَلَهُ سَتَجِدُنِی إِنْ شاءَ اللهُ صابِراً وَ لا أَعْصِی لَکَ أَمْراً وَ قَدْ کَانَ الْعَالِمُ یَعْلَمُ أَنَّ مُوسَی لَا یَصْبِرُ عَلَی عِلْمِهِ فَکَذَلِکَ وَ اللَّهِ یَا إِسْحَاقَ بْنَ عَمَّارٍ قُضَاةُ هَؤُلَاءِ وَ فُقَهَاؤُهُمْ وَ جَمَاعَتُهُمُ الْیَوْمَ لَا یَحْتَمِلُونَ وَ اللَّهِ عِلْمَنَا وَ لَا یَقْبَلُونَهُ وَ لَا یُطِیقُونَهُ وَ لَا یَأْخُذُونَ بِهِ وَ لَا یَصْبِرُونَ عَلَیْهِ کَمَا لَمْ یَصْبِرْ مُوسَی عَلَی عِلْمِ الْعَالِمِ حِینَ صَحِبَهُ وَ رَأَی مَا رَأَی مِنْ عِلْمِهِ وَ کَانَ ذَلِکَ عِنْدَ مُوسَی مَکْرُوهاً وَ کَانَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ رِضًا وَ هُوَ الْحَقُّ وَ کَذَلِکَ عِلْمُنَا عِنْدَ الْجَهَلَةِ مَکْرُوهٌ لَا یُؤْخَذُ وَ هُوَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ الْحَقُّ.
60.en: Ishaq ibn Ammar narrates that Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: "The likeness of Ali (peace be upon him) and us, the Imams after him from this Ummah, is like the likeness of Moses the Prophet and the Scholar (al-Khidr) when he met him, spoke with him, and asked for his companionship. The matter of their encounter is what God has recounted for His Prophet in His Book. God said to Moses: 'I have chosen you over the people with My messages and My speech, so take what I have given you and be among the grateful' (Al-A'raf: 144). Then He said: 'And We wrote for him on the tablets [something] of all things, an instruction and explanation for all things' (Al-A'raf: 145). The Scholar possessed knowledge that was not written for Moses on the tablets. Moses thought that all the things he needed and all knowledge had been written for him on the tablets, just as these people who claim to be jurists and scholars think—that they have established all the knowledge and jurisprudence in the religion that this Ummah needs, and that they have verified it from the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), learned it, and memorized it. But it is not so; they have not inherited all the knowledge of the Messenger of God, nor has it reached them from him, nor have they understood it. For when a matter of the lawful, the unlawful, and the rulings comes to them, they are asked about it, and they have no tradition from the Messenger of God regarding it. They are ashamed that people might attribute ignorance to them, and they dislike being asked and not being able to answer, which would lead people to seek knowledge from its true source. Therefore, they employ personal opinion (ra'y) and analogy (qiyas) in the religion of God, abandon the traditions (athar), and practice innovations (bid'ah) in the name of God, even though the Messenger of God said: 'Every innovation is a misguidance.' If, when asked about something in the religion of God for which they had no tradition from the Messenger of God, they had referred it to God, the Messenger, and those in authority among them, those who are able to derive it—the family of Muhammad—would have known it. But what prevents them from seeking knowledge from us is their enmity and envy toward us. By God, Moses did not envy the Scholar—even though Moses was a Prophet of God to whom revelation was sent—when he met him, spoke with him, and acknowledged his knowledge. He did not envy him as this Ummah has envied us after the Messenger of God regarding our knowledge and what we inherited from him. They do not desire to learn from us as Moses desired to learn from the Scholar and asked for his companionship to learn from him and be guided. When Moses asked the Scholar for that, the Scholar knew that Moses could not bear his companionship, could not endure his knowledge, and would not be patient with him. At that point, the Scholar said: 'And how can you have patience for what you do not encompass in knowledge?' Moses, in his humility, seeking to be accepted, said to him: 'You will find me, if God wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any matter.' Yet the Scholar knew that Moses would not be patient with his knowledge. So it is, by God, O Ishaq ibn Ammar, with these judges, jurists, and their followers today. By God, they cannot bear our knowledge, they do not accept it, they cannot endure it, they do not take from it, and they are not patient with it, just as Moses was not patient with the knowledge of the Scholar when he accompanied him and saw what he saw of his knowledge. That was disliked by Moses, but it was pleasing to God and was the truth. Likewise, our knowledge is disliked by the ignorant and is not accepted, but in the sight of God, it is the truth."
60.book: Tafsir Ahl al-Bayt (peace be upon them), Vol. 8, p. 534
60.refs: Bihar al-Anwar, Vol. 2, p. 208; Nur al-Thaqalayn.

60.ar: الصّادقین (- عَنْ بُرَیْدِ بْنِ مُعَاوِیَةَ عَنْ أَبِی جَعْفَرٍ وَ أَبِی عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ مَا مَنْزِلَتُکُمْ وَ مَنْ تُشْبِهُونَ مِمَّنْ مَضَی قَالَ صَاحِبُ مُوسَی (وَ ذُو الْقَرْنَیْنِ کَانَا عَالِمَیْنِ وَ لَمْ یَکُونَا نَبِیَّیْن.
60.fa: بریدبن‌معاویه گوید: از امام باقر یا امام صادق (علیها السلام) پرسیدم: «از بین گذشتگان، شما به کدام‌یک شباهت بیشتری دارید»؟ فرمود: «به خضر و ذوالقرنین که عالم بودند امّا پیامبر نبودند».
60.en: Burayd ibn Mu’awiyah said: I asked Abu Ja’far [al-Baqir] or Abu ‘Abd Allah [al-Sadiq] (peace be upon them), "What is your status, and whom among those who have passed do you resemble?" He replied, "The companion of Musa [al-Khidr] and Dhu al-Qarnayn; they were both learned men, but they were not prophets."
60.book: Tafsir Ahl al-Bayt (peace be upon them), Vol. 8, p. 536
60.refs: Al-Kafi, Vol. 1, p. 269; Nur al-Thaqalayn; Al-Burhan; (with slight variations)

60.ar: الباقر (- عَنْ حُمْرَانَ بْنِ أَعْیَنَ قَالَ قُلْتُ لِأَبِی جَعْفَرٍ (مَا مَوْضِعُ الْعُلَمَاءِ قَالَ مِثْلُ ذِی الْقَرْنَیْنِ وَ صَاحِبِ سُلَیْمَانَ (وَ صَاحِبِ مُوسَی (.
60.fa: حمران‌بن‌اعین گوید: به امام باقر (علیه السلام) عرض کردم: «موقعیّت علما چیست»؟ فرمود: «مانند ذی‌القرنین و رفیق سلیمان (علیه السلام) و دوست موسی (علیه السلام)».
60.en: Humran ibn A'yan said: I said to Abu Ja'far (al-Baqir), "What is the status of the scholars?" He replied, "Like Dhu al-Qarnayn, the companion of Solomon (peace be upon him), and the companion of Moses (peace be upon him)."
60.book: Tafsir Ahl al-Bayt (peace be upon them), Vol. 8, p. 536
60.refs: Mir'at al-'Uqul, Vol. 3, p. 156; Nur al-Thaqalayn; in it: "and the companion of Solomon" is omitted.

60.ar: الباقر (- عَنْ حُمْرَانَ بْنِ أَعْیَنَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ (إِنَّ عَلِیّاً (کَانَ مُحَدَّثاً فَخَرَجْتُ إِلَی أَصْحَابِی فَقُلْتُ جِئْتُکُمْ بِعَجِیبَةٍ فَقَالُوا وَ مَا هِیَ فَقُلْتُ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ (یَقُولُ کَانَ عَلِیٌّ (مُحَدَّثاً فَقَالُوا مَا صَنَعْتَ شَیْئاً إِلَّا سَأَلْتَهُ مَنْ کَانَ یُحَدِّثُهُ فَرَجَعْتُ إِلَیْهِ فَقُلْتُ إِنِّی حَدَّثْتُ أَصْحَابِی بِمَا حَدَّثْتَنِی فَقَالُوا مَا صَنَعْتَ شَیْئاً إِلَّا سَأَلْتَهُ مَنْ کَانَ یُحَدِّثُهُ فَقَالَ لِی یُحَدِّثُهُ مَلَکٌ قُلْتُ تَقُولُ إِنَّهُ نَبِیٌّ قَالَ فَحَرَّکَ یَدَهُ هَکَذَا أَوْ کَصَاحِبِ سُلَیْمَانَ (أَوْ کَصَاحِبِ مُوسَی (أَوْ کَذِی الْقَرْنَیْنِ أَ وَ مَا بَلَغَکُمْ أَنَّهُ قَالَ وَ فِیکُمْ مِثْلُهُ.
60.fa: حمران‌بن‌اعین گوید: امام باقر (علیه السلام) فرمود: «به‌راستی علی (علیه السلام) محدَّث بود»، این را به رفقایم خبر دادم، گفتند: «تا از او نپرسی چه کسی به او حدیث می‌گوید، کاری نکرده‌ای». به‌سوی امام (علیه السلام) برگشتم و گفته‌ی آنان را بازگو کردم. حضرت به من فرمود: «فرشته‌ای با او حدیث می‌گوید». عرض کردم: «مگر علی (علیه السلام) پیغمبر است»؟ فرمود: «نه. بلکه مانند یار و همدم سلیمان (علیه السلام)، یعنی آصف‌بن‌برخیا و همدم موسی (علیه السلام) و یا همچون ذوالقرنین، مگر به شما نرسیده که [پیامبر (صلی الله علیه و آله)] فرمود: «در میان شما مانند و شبیه او (ذوالقرنین) وجود دارد».
60.en: Humran ibn A'yan said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said, "Verily, Ali (peace be upon him) was a muhaddath (one who is spoken to by angels)." I went out to my companions and said, "I have brought you a wonder." They asked, "And what is it?" I said, "I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) say, 'Ali (peace be upon him) was a muhaddath.'" They replied, "You have accomplished nothing unless you ask him who it was that spoke to him." I returned to him and said, "I told my companions what you told me, and they said, 'You have accomplished nothing unless you ask him who it was that spoke to him.'" He said to me, "An angel speaks to him." I asked, "Are you saying that he is a prophet?" He gestured with his hand like this, or [he said], "Like the companion of Sulayman (peace be upon him), or like the companion of Musa (peace be upon him), or like Dhu al-Qarnayn. Has it not reached you that he [the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)] said, 'And among you is his like'?"
60.book: Tafsir Ahl al-Bayt (peace be upon them), Vol. 8, p. 536
60.refs: Al-Kafi, Vol. 1, p. 271; Nur al-Thaqalayn; [with slight variations]

61.ar: الصّادقین (- لَمَّا کَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ مُوسَی (الَّذِی کَانَ أُعْطِیَ مِکْتَلًا فِیهِ حُوتٌ مَالِحٌ فَقِیلَ لَهُ هَذَا یَدُلُّکَ عَلَی صَاحِب-ِکَ عِنْدَ عَیْ-نٍ لَا یُصِیبُ مِنْهَا شَیْءٌ إِلَّا حَیَّ فَانْطَلَقَا حَتَّی بَلَغَا الصَّخْرَةَ وَ جَاوَزَا ثُمَّ قالَ لِفَتاهُ آتِنا غَداءَنا فَقَالَ الْحُوتُ اتَّخَذَ فِی الْبَحْرِ سَرَباً فَاقْتَصَّا الْأَثَرَ حَتَّی أَتَیَا صَاحِبَهُمَا فِی جَزِیرَةٍ فِی کِسَاءٍ جَالِساً فَسَلَّمَ عَلَیْه.
61.fa: چون به موسی (علیه السلام) سبدی که در آن ماهی شور قرار داشت دادند به او گفته شد: «این ماهی تو را راهنمایی می‌کند به دوستی که در جستجوی او هستی نزدیک آن چشمه‌ای که یک مختصر از آب آن اگر به ماهی رسید، زنده می‌شود». موسی (علیه السلام) و همراهش رفتند تا رسیدند به آن سنگ و از آن رد شدند موسی (علیه السلام) به آن جوان گفت: «غذای ما را بیاور» در جواب موسی (علیه السلام) گفت: «ماهی راه خود را در دریا پیش گرفت (و روان شد)». به‌دنبال آن نشانه رفتند تا رسیدند به آن کسی که باید او را ملاقات کنند در جزیره‌ای بود داخل کسایی نشسته بود سلام کردند.
61.en: When Moses (peace be upon him) was given a basket containing a salted fish, he was told: "This fish will guide you to your companion whom you are seeking, near a spring where anything that touches its water comes to life." They set out until they reached the rock and passed it. Then Moses (peace be upon him) said to his young attendant, "Bring us our lunch." In response, [the attendant] said to Moses (peace be upon him), "The fish has taken its path into the sea." They retraced their steps until they reached their companion on an island, sitting wrapped in a cloak, and they greeted him.
61.book: Tafsir Ahl al-Bayt (peace be upon them), Vol. 8, p. 536

62.ar: الصّادقین (- لَمَّا کَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ مُوسَی (الَّذِی کَانَ أُعْطِیَ مکتل {مِکْتَلًا} فِیهِ حُوتٌ مُمَلَّحٌ وَ قِیلَ لَهُ هَذَا یَدُلُّکُ عَلَی صَاحِبِکَ عِنْدَ عَیْنِ مَجْمَعِ الْبَحْرَیْنِ لَا یُصِیبُ مِنْهَا شَیْءٌ مَیِّتاً إِلَّا حَیِیَ یُقَالُ لَهُ الْحَیَاةُ فَانْطَلَقَا حَتَّی بَلَغَا الصَّخْرَةَ فَانْطَلَقَ الْفَتَی یَغْسِلُ الْحُوتَ فِی الْعَیْنِ فَاضْطَرَبَ فِی یَدِهِ حَتَّی خَدَشَهُ وَ انْفَلَتَ مِنْهُ وَ نَسِیَهُ الْفَتَی فَلَمَّا جَاوَزَ الْوَقْتَ الَّذِی وُقِّتَ فِیهِ أَعْیَا مُوسَی (وَ قَالَ لِفَتَاهُ آتِنا غَداءَنا لَقَدْ لَقِینا مِنْ سَفَرِنا هذا نَصَباً قالَ أَ رَأَیْتَ إِلَی قَوْلِهِ عَلی آثارِهِما قَصَصاً فَلَمَّا أَتَاهَا وَجَدَ الْحُوتَ قَدْ خَرَّ فِی الْبَحْرِ فَاقْتَصَّا الْأَثَرَ حَتَّی أَتَیَا صَاحِبَهُمَا فِی جَزِیرَةٍ مِنْ جَزَائِرِ الْبَحْرِ إِمَّا مُتَّکِئاً وَ إِمَّا جَالِساً فِی کِسَاءٍ لَهُ فَسَلَّمَ عَلَیْهِ مُوسَی (فَعَجِبَ مِنَ السَّلَامِ.
62.fa: وقتی امر موسی (علیه السلام) - که زنبیلی به او داده شده بود و در آن ماهی شوری بود - واقع شد [و قرار شد موسی (علیه السلام) با عالم دیدار کند] به موسی (علیه السلام) گفته شد: «این [ماهی]، تو را نزد چشمه‌ای که در محلّ تلاقی دو دریا است بر دوستت راهنمایی می‌کند. چیزی از آن [چشمه] بر مرده‌ای نمی‌رسد مگر آنکه زنده می‌شود. به آن، [چشمه] «زندگانی» می‌گویند. موسی (علیه السلام) و جوان همراهش به راه افتادند تا اینکه به سنگ رسیدند، جوانِ [همراه موسی (علیه السلام)] رفت تا ماهی را در چشمه بشوید که ماهی [زنده شد و] در دستش لرزید و تکان خورد تا اینکه آن را خراشید و از آن رها شد و جوان فراموش کرد [که جریان را به موسی (علیه السلام) بگوید] و هنگامی‌که زمان تعیین شده [برای دیدار با عالم] گذشت، موسی (علیه السلام) خسته و درمانده شد و فرمود: «لِفَتَاهُ آتِنا غَداءَنا لَقَدْ لَقِینا مِنْ سَفَرِنا هذا نَصَباً». گفت: قَالَ أَ رَءَیْتَ إِذْ أَوَیْنَا إِلیَ الصَّخْرَةِ فَإِنیّ‌ِ نَسِیتُ الحْوتَ وَ مَا أَنسَئنِیهُ إِلَّا الشَّیْطَنُ أَنْ أَذْکُرَهُ وَ اتخَّذَ سَبِیلَهُ فیِ الْبَحْرِ عجَبًا* قَالَ ذَالِکَ مَا کُنَّا نَبْغِ فَارْتَدَّا عَلیَ ءَاثَارِهِمَا قَصَصًا؛ پس به‌دنبال او رفتند تا اینکه نزد دوستشان - در جزیره‌ای از جزایر دریا - آمدند. در پوششی که داشت یا تکیه کرده بود یا نشسته بود. موسی (علیه السلام) به او سلام کرد و او از سلام تعجّب کرد».
62.en: When the matter of Moses (peace be upon him) occurred—he had been given a basket containing a salted fish, and it was said to him: "This will guide you to your companion at the spring at the junction of the two seas; nothing dead touches it but it becomes alive; it is called the [Spring of] Life"—they set out until they reached the rock. The young man went to wash the fish in the spring, and it thrashed in his hand until it scratched him and escaped. The young man forgot [to mention it to Moses]. When they passed the appointed time, Moses became exhausted and said to his servant: "Bring us our morning meal; indeed, we have suffered much fatigue from this journey of ours." He [the servant] said: "Did you see when we retired to the rock? Indeed, I forgot the fish, and none made me forget it except Satan, that I should mention it. And it took its course into the sea, amazingly." He said: "That is what we were seeking." So they returned, retracing their footsteps, until they came to their companion on one of the islands of the sea. He was either reclining or sitting in a garment he had. Moses greeted him, and he was surprised by the greeting.
62.book: Tafsir Ahl al-Bayt (peace be upon them), Vol. 8, p. 538
62.refs: Bihar al-Anwar, Vol. 13, p. 305; Al-Ayyashi, Vol. 2, p. 329; "He said: Did you see... to the end" is omitted.

62.ar: الباقر (- شَکَا مُوسَی (إِلَی رَبِّهِ الْجُوعَ فِی ثَلَاثَةِ مَوَاضِعَ آتِنا غَداءَنا لَقَدْ لَقِینا مِنْ سَفَرِنا هذا نَصَباً، لَاتَّخَذْتَ عَلَیْهِ أَجْراً، رَبِّ إِنِّی لِما أَنْزَلْتَ إِلَیَّ مِنْ خَیْرٍ فَقِیرٌ.
62.en: Moses complained to his Lord about hunger in three instances: "Bring us our morning meal; we have certainly suffered much fatigue from this journey of ours" (Kahf/62), "[At least] you could have taken a wage for it" (Kahf/77), and "My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You would send down to me, in need" (Qasas/24).
62.book: Tafsir Ahl al-Bayt (peace be upon them), Vol. 8, p. 538
62.refs: Bihar al-Anwar, Vol. 13, p. 309; al-Ayyashi, Vol. 2, p. 335; Nur al-Thaqalayn; al-Burhan

62.ar: الصّادق (- عَنْ حَفْصِ بْنِ الْبَخْتَرِیِّ عَنْ أَبِی عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (فِی قَوْلِ مُوسَی (لِفَتَاهُ آتِنا غَداءَنا وَ قَوْلِهِ رَبِّ إِنِّی لِما أَنْزَلْتَ إِلَیَّ مِنْ خَیْرٍ فَقِیرٌ فَقَالَ إِنَّمَا عَنَی الطَّعَامَ فَقَالَ أَبِی عَبْدِاللَّهِ (إِنَّ مُوسَی (لَذُو جُوعَاتٍ.
62.en: Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari narrates: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said regarding the words of Moses (peace be upon him) to his servant, "Bring us our morning meal," and his words, "My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You would send down to me, in need," that he meant food. The Imam (peace be upon him) said, "Moses (peace be upon him) would often become very hungry."
62.book: Tafsir Ahl al-Bayt (peace be upon them), Vol. 8, p. 538
62.refs: Bihar al-Anwar, Vol. 13, p. 303; al-Ayyashi, Vol. 2, p. 330; Qisas al-Anbiya by al-Jaza'iri, p. 299; Nur al-Thaqalayn; al-Burhan

62.ar: ابن عبّاس (- عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ قَالَ: مَا وَجَدْتُ لِلنَّاسِ وَ لِعَلِیِّ بْنِ أَبِی طَالِبٍ (شَبَهاً إِلَّا مُوسَی (وَ صَاحِبَ السَّفِینَةِ تَکَلَّمَ مُوسَی (بِجَهْلٍ وَ تَکَلَّمَ صَاحِبُ السَّفِینَةِ بِعِلْمٍ وَ تَکَلَّمَ النَّاسُ بِجَهْلٍ وَ تَکَلَّمَ عَلِیٌّ (بِعِلْمٍ.
62.fa: از ابن‌عبّاس (رحمة الله علیه) روایت است: «مثَل مردم و علیّ‌بن‌ابی‌طالب (علیه السلام) مثَل موسی (علیه السلام) و صاحب کشتی است. موسی (علیه السلام) از روی نادانی سخن می‌گفت و صاحب کشتی از روی علم و آگاهی. این مردم نیز از روی نادانی سخن می‌گویند و علی (علیه السلام) از روی علم و آگاهی».
62.en: Ibn Abbas said: "I have found no likeness for the people and Ali ibn Abi Talib except for Moses and the owner of the ship. Moses spoke out of ignorance, while the owner of the ship spoke out of knowledge. These people speak out of ignorance, while Ali speaks out of knowledge."
62.book: Tafsir Ahl al-Bayt (peace be upon them), Vol. 8, p. 538

62.ar: ابن عبّاس (- عَنْ عَبَایَةَ الْأَسَدِیِّ قَالَ: کَانَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ الْعَبَّاسِ (جَالِساً عَلَی شَفِیرِ زَمْزَمَ یُحَدِّثُ النَّاسَ فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ مِنْ حَدِیثِهِ أَتَاهُ رَجُلٌ فَسَلَّمَ عَلَیْهِ ثُمَّ قَالَ: یَا عَبْدَ اللَّهِ، إِنِّی رَجُلٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الشَّامِ. فَقَالَ: أَعْوَانُ کُلِّ ظَالِمٍ إِلَّا مَنْ عَصَمَ اللَّهُ مِنْکُمْ، سَلْ عَمَّا بَدَا لَکَ. فَقَالَ: یَا عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عَبَّاسٍ، إِنِّی جِئْتُکَ أَسْأَلُکَ عَمَّنْ قَتَلَهُ عَلِیُّ بْنُ أَبِی طَالِبٍ (مِنْ أَهْلِ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ لَمْ یَکْفُرُوا بِصَلَاةٍ وَ لَا بِحَجٍّ وَ لَا بِصَوْمِ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ وَ لَا بِزَکَاةٍ؟ فَقَالَ لَهُ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: ثَکِلَتْکَ أُمُّکَ سَلْ عَمَّا یَعْنِیکَ وَ دَعْ مَا لَا یَعْنِیکَ. فَقَالَ: مَا جِئْتُکَ أَضْرِبُ إِلَیْکَ مِنْ حِمْصَ لِلْحَجِّ وَ لَا لِلْعُمْرَةِ وَ لَکِنِّی أَتَیْتُکَ لِتَشْرَحَ لِی أَمْرَ عَلِیِّ بْنِ أَبِی طَالِبٍ (وَ فِعَالَهُ. فَقَالَ لَهُ: وَیْلَکَ إِنَّ عِلْمَ الْعَالِمِ صَعْبٌ لَا تَحْتَمِلُهُ وَ لَا تَقْرَبُهُ الْقُلُوبُ الصَّدِئَةُ أُخْبِرُکَ أَنَّ عَلِیَّ بْنَ أَبِی طَالِبٍ (کَانَ مَثَلُهُ فِی هَذِهِ الْأُمَّةِ کَمَثَلِ مُوسَی (وَ الْعَالِمِ (وَ ذَلِکَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ تَبَارَکَ وَ تَعَالَی قَالَ فِی کِتَابِهِ یا مُوسَی إِنِّی اصْطَفَیْتُکَ عَلَی النَّاسِ بِرِسالاتِی وَ بِکَلامِی فَخُذْ ما آتَیْتُکَ وَ کُنْ مِنَ الشَّاکِرِینَ وَ کَتَبْنا لَهُ فِی الْأَلْواحِ مِنْ کُلِّ شَیْءٍ مَوْعِظَةً وَ تَفْصِیلًا لِکُلِّ شَیْءٍ فَکَانَ مُوسَی (یَرَی أَنَّ جَمِیعَ الْأَشْیَاءِ قَدْ أُثْبِتَتْ لَهُ کَمَا تَرَوْنَ أَنْتُمْ أَنَّ عُلَمَاءَکُمْ قَدْ أَثْبَتُوا جَمِیعَ الْأَشْیَاءِ فَلَمَّا انْتَهَی مُوسَی (إِلَی سَاحِلِ الْبَحْرِ فَلَقِیَ الْعَالِمَ فَاسْتَنْطَقَ بِمُوسَی (لِیَصِلَ عِلْمَهُ وَ لَمْ یَحْسُدْهُ کَمَا حَسَدْتُمْ أَنْتُمْ عَلِیَّ بْنَ أَبِی طَالِبٍ (وَ أَنْکَرْتُمْ فَضْلَهُ فَقَالَ لَهُ مُوسَی (هَلْ أَتَّبِعُکَ عَلی أَنْ تُعَلِّمَنِ مِمَّا عُلِّمْتَ رُشْداً؟ فَعَلِمَ الْعَالِمُ أَنَّ مُوسَی (لَا یُطِیقُ بِصُحْبَتِهِ وَ لَا یَصْبِرُ عَلَی عِلْمِهِ فَقَالَ لَهُ إِنَّکَ لَنْ تَسْتَطِیعَ مَعِیَ صَبْراً وَ کَیْفَ تَصْبِرُ عَلی ما لَمْ تُحِطْ بِهِ خُبْراً فَقَالَ لَهُ مُوسَی (سَتَجِدُنِی إِنْ شاءَ اللهُ صابِراً وَ لا أَعْصِی لَکَ أَمْراً فَعَلِمَ الْعَالِمُ أَنَّ مُوسَی (لَا یَصْبِرُ عَلَی عِلْمِهِ فَقَالَ فَإِنِ اتَّبَعْتَنِی فَلا تَسْئَلْنِی عَنْ شَیْءٍ حَتَّی أُحْدِثَ لَکَ مِنْهُ ذِکْراً قَالَ فَرَکِبَا فِی السَّفِینَةِ فَخَرَقَهَا الْعَالِمُ وَ کَانَ خَرْقُهَا لِلَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ رِضًی وَ سَخِطَ ذَلِکَ مُوسَی (وَ لَقِیَ الْغُلَامَ فَقَتَلَهُ فَکَانَ قَتْلُهُ لِلَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ رِضًی وَ سَخِطَ ذَلِکَ مُوسَی (وَ أَقَامَ الْجِدَارَ فَکَانَ إِقَامَتُهُ لِلَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ رِضًی وَ سَخِطَ ذَلِکَ مُوسَی (کَذَلِکَ کَانَ عَلِیُّ بْنُ أَبِی طَالِبٍ (لَمْ یَقْتُلْ إِلَّا مَنْ کَانَ قَتْلُهُ لِلَّهِ رِضًی وَ لِأَهْلِ الْجَهَالَةِ مِنَ النَّاسِ سَخَطاً.
62.en: Abayah al-Asadi narrated: Abdullah ibn Abbas (may Allah have mercy on him) was sitting at the edge of the Zamzam well, speaking to the people. When he finished his discourse, a man came to him, greeted him, and said, "O Abdullah, I am a man from the people of Sham (Syria)." Abdullah replied, "You are all helpers of every oppressor, except for those among you whom Allah has protected. Ask whatever comes to your mind." The man said, "O Abdullah ibn Abbas, I have come to you to ask about those whom Ali ibn Abi Talib killed—people who testified that there is no god but Allah, who did not disbelieve in prayer, nor pilgrimage, nor fasting the month of Ramadan, nor in Zakat." Abdullah said to him, "May your mother mourn you! Ask about what concerns you and leave what does not concern you." The man said, "I did not come to you all the way from Homs for the sake of Hajj or Umrah; rather, I came so that you might explain to me the affair of Ali ibn Abi Talib and his actions." He said to him, "Woe to you! The knowledge of the 'knower' (al-alim) is difficult; hearts that are rusted cannot bear it, nor can they approach it. I will tell you that the likeness of Ali ibn Abi Talib in this nation is like the likeness of Moses and the 'knower' (al-Khidr). This is because Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, said in His Book: 'O Moses, I have chosen you over the people with My messages and My speech. So take what I have given you and be among the grateful.' And We wrote for him on the tablets [something] of all things—instruction and explanation for all things. Moses thought that all things had been established for him, just as you think that your scholars have established all things. When Moses reached the seashore and met the 'knower,' he sought to learn from him to attain his knowledge, and he did not envy him as you have envied Ali ibn Abi Talib and denied his excellence. Moses said to him, 'May I follow you on [the condition] that you teach me from what you have been taught of sound judgment?' The 'knower' knew that Moses would not be able to accompany him and would not have patience for his knowledge, so he said to him, 'Indeed, with me you will never be able to have patience. And how can you have patience for what you do not encompass in knowledge?' Moses said to him, 'You will find me, if Allah wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any matter.' The 'knower' knew that Moses would not have patience for his knowledge, so he said, 'Then if you follow me, do not ask me about anything until I make to you about it mention.' He said: So they boarded the ship, and the 'knower' breached it. His breaching of it was for the pleasure of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, yet Moses was angered by it. He met the boy and killed him; his killing of him was for the pleasure of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, yet Moses was angered by it. He restored the wall; his restoration of it was for the pleasure of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, yet Moses was angered by it. Likewise was Ali ibn Abi Talib; he did not kill anyone except those whose killing was for the pleasure of Allah, while the ignorant people were angered by it."
62.book: Tafsir Ahl al-Bayt (peace be upon them), Vol. 8, p. 540

65.ar: الصّادق (- فَمَضَی هُوَ وَ فَتَاهُ یوشع بن نون (حَتَّی انْتَهَیَا إِلَی مُلْتَقَی الْبَحْرَیْنِ فَوَجَدَا هُنَاکَ الخِضْر (یَتَعَبَّدُ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ کَمَا قَالَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ فَوَجَدا عَبْداً مِنْ عِبادِنا آتَیْناهُ رَحْمَةً مِنْ عِنْدِنا وَعَلَّمْناهُ مِنْ لَدُنَّا عِلْما.
65.fa: موسی (علیه السلام) و رفیق جوانمردش که خدمتکار و وصیّ او بود موسوم به یوشع‌بن‌نون حرکت کردند تا به مجمع‌البحرین رسیدند در آنجا خضر (علیه السلام) را یافتند که عبادت حقّ تبارک‌وتعالی را می‌نمود چنانچه خدای عزّوجلّ در کتابش می‌فرماید: فَوَجَدا عَبْداً مِنْ عِبادِنا آتَیْناهُ رَحْمَةً مِنْ عِنْدِنا وَ عَلَّمْناهُ مِنْ لَدُنَّا عِلْماً.
65.en: He and his young companion, Joshua son of Nun, set out until they reached the junction of the two seas. There, they found al-Khidr worshipping Allah, the Almighty and Majestic, just as Allah, the Almighty and Majestic, says: "And they found a servant from among Our servants to whom We had given mercy from Us and had taught him from Us a [certain] knowledge."
65.book: Tafsir Ahl al-Bayt (peace be upon them), Vol. 8, p. 542
65.refs: Bihar al-Anwar, Vol. 13, p. 286 / 'Ilal al-Shara'i', Vol. 1, p. 59

65.ar: الصّادق (- عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِی عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (قَالَ: إِنَّمَا مَثَلُ عَلِیٍّ (وَ مَثَلُنَا مِنْ بَعْدِهِ مِنْ هَذِهِ الْأُمَّةِ کَمَثَلِ مُوسَی النَّبِیِّ عَلَی نَبِیِّنَا وَ آلِهِ وَ (وَ الْعَالِمِ حِینَ لَقِیَهُ وَ اسْتَنْطَقَهُ وَ سَأَلَهُ الصُّحْبَةَ فَکَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِهِمَا مَا اقْتَصَّهُ اللَّهُ لِنَبِیِّهِ (فِی کِتَابِهِ وَ ذَلِکَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ قَالَ لِمُوسَی إِنِّی اصْطَفَیْتُکَ عَلَی النَّاسِ بِرِسالاتِی وَ بِکَلامِی فَخُذْ ما آتَیْتُکَ وَ کُنْ مِنَ الشَّاکِرِینَ ثُمَّ قَالَ وَ کَتَبْنا لَهُ فِی الْأَلْواحِ مِنْ کُلِّ شَیْءٍ مَوْعِظَةً وَ تَفْصِیلًا لِکُلِّ شَیْءٍ وَ قَدْ کَانَ عِنْدَ الْعَالِمِ عِلْمٌ لَمْ یُکْتَبْ لِمُوسَی فِی الْأَلْوَاحِ وَ کَانَ مُوسَی یَظُنُّ أَنَّ جَمِیعَ الْأَشْیَاءِ الَّتِی یَحْتَاجُ إِلَیْهَا وَ جَمِیعَ الْعِلْمِ قَدْ کُتِبَ لَهُ فِی الْأَلْوَاحِ کَمَا یَظُنُّ هَؤُلَاءِ الَّذِینَ یَدَّعُونَ أَنَّهُمْ فُقَهَاءُ وَ عُلَمَاءُ وَ أَنَّهُمْ قَدْ أَثْبَتُوا جَمِیعَ الْعِلْمِ وَ الْفِقْهِ فِی الدِّینِ مِمَّا یَحْتَاجُ هَذِهِ الْأُمَّةُ إِلَیْهِ وَ صَحَّ لَهُمْ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ (وَ عَلِمُوهُ وَ لَفَظُوهُ وَ لَیْسَ کُلُّ عِلْمِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ (عَلِمُوهُ وَ لَا صَارَ إِلَیْهِمْ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ (وَ لَا عَرَفُوهُ وَ ذَلِکَ أَنَّ الشَّیْءَ مِنَ الْحَلَالِ وَ الْحَرَامِ وَ الْأَحْکَامِ یَرِدُ عَلَیْهِمْ فَیُسْأَلُونَ عَنْهُ وَ لَا یَکُونُ عِنْدَهُمْ فِیهِ أَثَرٌ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ (وَ یَسْتَحْیُونَ أَنْ یَنْسُبَهُمُ النَّاسُ إِلَی الْجَهْلِ وَ یَکْرَهُونَ أَنْ یُسْأَلُوا فَلَا یُجِیبُوا فَیَطْلُبَ النَّاسُ الْعِلْمَ مِنْ مَعْدِنِهِ فَلِذَلِکَ اسْتَعْمَلُوا الرَّأْیَ وَ الْقِیَاسَ فِی دِینِ اللَّهِ وَ تَرَکُوا الْآثَارَ وَ دَانُوا لِلَّهِ بِالْبِدَعِ وَ قَدْ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ (کُلُّ بِدْعَةٍ ضَلَالَةٌ فَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ إِذْ سُئِلُوا عَنْ شَیْءٍ مِنْ دِینِ اللَّهِ فَلَمْ یَکُنْ عِنْدَهُمْ مِنْهُ أَثَرٌ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ (رَدُّوهُ إِلَی اللَّهِ وَ إِلَی الرَّسُولِ وَ إِلی أُولِی الْأَمْرِ مِنْهُمْ لَعَلِمَهُ الَّذِینَ یَسْتَنْبِطُونَهُ مِنْهُمْ مِنْ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ الَّذِینَ مَنَعَهُمْ مِنْ طَلَبِ الْعِلْمِ مِنَّا الْعَدَاوَةُ وَ الْحَسَدُ لَنَا وَ لَا وَ اللَّهِ مَا حَسَدَ مُوسَی الْعَالِمَ وَ مُوسَی نَبِیُّ اللَّهِ یُوحَی إِلَیْهِ حَیْثُ لَقِیَهُ وَ اسْتَنْطَقَهُ وَ عَرَفَهُ بِالْعِلْمِ وَ لَمْ یَحْسُدْهُ کَمَا حَسَدَتْنَا هَذِهِ الْأُمَّةُ بَعْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ (عِلْمَنَا وَ مَا وَرِثْنَا عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ (وَ لَمْ یَرْغَبُوا إِلَیْنَا فِی عِلْمِنَا کَمَا رَغِبَ مُوسَی إِلَی الْعَالِمِ وَ سَأَلَهُ الصُّحْبَةَ لِیَتَعَلَّمَ مِنْهُ الْعِلْمَ وَ یُرْشِدَهُ فَلَمَّا أَنْ سَأَلَ الْعَالِمَ ذَلِکَ عَلِمَ الْعَالِمُ أَنَّ مُوسَی لَا یَسْتَطِیعُ صُحْبَتَهُ وَ لَا یَحْتَمِلُ عِلْمَهُ وَ لَا یَصْبِرُ مَعَهُ فَعِنْدَ ذَلِکَ قَالَ الْعَالِمُ وَ کَیْفَ تَصْبِرُ عَلی ما لَمْ تُحِطْ بِهِ خُبْراً فَقَالَ لَهُ مُوسَی وَ هُوَ خَاضِعٌ لَهُ یَسْتَنْطِقُهُ عَلَی نَفْسِهِ کَیْ یَقْبَلَهُ سَتَجِدُنِی إِنْ شاءَ اللهُ صابِراً وَ لا أَعْصِی لَکَ أَمْراً وَ قَدْ کَانَ الْعَالِمُ یَعْلَمُ أَنَّ مُوسَی لَا یَصْبِرُ عَلَی عِلْمِهِ فَکَذَلِکَ وَ اللَّهِ یَا إِسْحَاقَ بْنَ عَمَّارٍ قُضَاةُ هَؤُلَاءِ وَ فُقَهَاؤُهُمْ وَ جَمَاعَتُهُمُ الْیَوْمَ لَا یَحْتَمِلُونَ وَ اللَّهِ عِلْمَنَا وَ لَا یَقْبَلُونَهُ وَ لَا یُطِیقُونَهُ وَ لَا یَأْخُذُونَ بِهِ وَ لَا یَصْبِرُونَ عَلَیْهِ کَمَا لَمْ یَصْبِرْ مُوسَی عَلَی عِلْمِ الْعَالِمِ حِینَ صَحِبَهُ وَ رَأَی مَا رَأَی مِنْ عِلْمِهِ وَ کَانَ ذَلِکَ عِنْدَ مُوسَی مَکْرُوهاً وَ کَانَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ رِضًا وَ هُوَ الْحَقُّ وَ کَذَلِکَ عِلْمُنَا عِنْدَ الْجَهَلَةِ مَکْرُوهٌ لَا یُؤْخَذُ وَ هُوَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ الْحَقُّ.
65.en: Ishaq ibn Ammar narrates: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: "The likeness of Ali (peace be upon him) and us, the Imams after him from this nation, is like the likeness of Moses and the Scholar (al-Khidr) (peace be upon them) when Moses met him, spoke with him, and asked for his companionship. The story of their affair is what God related to His Prophet (blessings of God be upon him and his family) in His Book. God said to Moses: 'I have chosen you above the people with My messages and My speech, so take what I have given you and be among the grateful' (Al-A'raf/144). Then He said: 'And We wrote for him in the tablets an admonition of everything and a detailed explanation of all things' (Al-A'raf/144). The Scholar possessed knowledge that was not written for Moses in the tablets. Moses thought that all the things he needed and all knowledge had been written for him in the tablets, just as these people who claim to be jurists and scholars think—that they have established all the knowledge and jurisprudence in the religion that this nation needs, and that they have correctly received it from the Messenger of God (blessings of God be upon him and his family), learned it, and memorized it. But they have not learned all the knowledge of the Messenger of God, nor has it all reached them, nor have they known it. For when a matter of the lawful, the unlawful, and the rulings comes to them, they are asked about it, and they have no tradition from the Messenger of God regarding it. They are ashamed that people might attribute ignorance to them, and they dislike being asked and not being able to answer, so that people might seek knowledge from its true source. Therefore, they employ personal opinion and analogy in the religion of God, abandon the traditions, and practice innovation in the name of God, even though the Messenger of God said: 'Every innovation is a misguidance.' If, when they were asked about something in the religion of God and had no tradition from the Messenger of God, they had referred it to God, the Messenger, and those in authority among them, those who derive knowledge from them—the family of Muhammad—would have known it. But what prevents them from seeking knowledge from us is enmity and envy toward us. By God, Moses did not envy the Scholar—even though Moses was a Prophet of God to whom revelation was sent—when he met him, spoke with him, and recognized his knowledge. He did not envy him as this nation has envied us after the Messenger of God regarding our knowledge and what we inherited from him. They do not desire to learn from us as Moses desired to learn from the Scholar and asked for his companionship to learn from him and be guided. When Moses asked the Scholar for that, the Scholar knew that Moses could not bear his companionship, could not endure his knowledge, and would not be patient with him. At that point, the Scholar said: 'And how can you have patience about things whose knowledge you do not encompass?' (Al-Kahf/68). Moses, in his humility and seeking to convince him to accept him, said: 'You will find me, if God wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any matter' (Al-Kahf/69). But the Scholar knew that Moses would not be patient with his knowledge. So it is, by God, O Ishaq ibn Ammar, with these judges, jurists, and their masses today. By God, they cannot bear our knowledge, they do not accept it, they cannot endure it, they do not take from it, and they are not patient with it, just as Moses was not patient with the knowledge of the Scholar when he accompanied him and saw what he saw of his knowledge. That was disliked by Moses, but it was pleasing to God, and it is the truth. Likewise, our knowledge is disliked by the ignorant and is not accepted, yet it is the truth in the sight of God."
65.book: Tafsir Ahl al-Bayt (peace be upon them), Vol. 8, p. 542

65.ar: الصّادق (- عَنْ سَیْفٍ التَّمَّارِ قَالَ: کُنَّا مَعَ أَبِی عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (جَمَاعَةً مِنَ الشِّیعَةِ فِی الْحِجْرِ فَقَالَ عَلَیْنَا عَیْنٌ فَالْتَفَتْنَا یَمْنَةً وَ یَسْرَةً فَلَمْ نَرَ أَحَداً فَقُلْنَا لَیْسَ عَلَیْنَا عَیْنٌ قَالَ وَ رَبِّ الْکَعْبَةِ وَ رَبِّ الْبَیْتِ ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ لَوْ کُنْتُ بَیْنَ مُوسَی وَ الخِضْر لَأَخْبَرْتُهُمَا أَنِّی أَعْلَمُ مِنْهُمَا وَ لَأَنْبَأْتُهُمَا بِمَا لَیْسَ فِی أَیْدِیهِمَا لِأَنَّ مُوسَی وَ الخِضْر أُعْطِیَا عِلْمَ مَا کَانَ وَ لَمْ یُعْطَیَا عِلْمَ مَا هُوَ کَائِنٌ إِلَی یَوْمِ الْقِیَامَةِ وَ إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أُعْطِیَ عِلْمَ مَا کَانَ وَ مَا هُوَ کَائِنٌ إِلَی یَوْمِ الْقِیَامَةِ فَوَرِثْنَاهُ مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ (وِرَاثَة.
65.fa: سیف تمّار گوید: با گروهی از شیعیان با امام صادق (علیه السلام) در حجر نشسته بودیم که ایشان فرمود: «یک چشم - جاسوس - به ما نگاه می کند»، به راست و چپ خود نگاه کردیم ولی کسی را ندیدیم. گفتیم: «کسی به ما نگاه نمی کند». سه بار فرمود: «قسم به خدای کعبه، قسم به خدای آن خانه، اگر بین موسی و خضر (علیها السلام) بودم به آنها خبر می‌دادم که من از آن‌ها عالم‌تر هستم و به آنچه در دستانشان نبود خبر می‌دادم. چون علم آنچه که اتفاق افتاده به آن‌ها داده شده ولی به آنها علم حوادث آینده و آنچه تا روز قیامت اتفاق می‌افتد داده نشده و ما اهل بیت این علم را از پیامبر (صلی الله علیه و آله) به ارث برده‌ایم».
65.en: Sayf al-Tammar said: We were with Abu Abd Allah (Imam al-Sadiq) along with a group of the Shia in the Hijr (of the Kaaba) when he said, "There is a spy watching us." We looked to our right and left but did not see anyone, so we said, "There is no one watching us." He said, "By the Lord of the Kaaba, by the Lord of the House," (repeating it three times), "If I were between Moses and al-Khidr, I would inform them that I am more knowledgeable than both of them, and I would inform them of what is not in their possession. For Moses and al-Khidr were given the knowledge of what has been, but they were not given the knowledge of what is to come until the Day of Resurrection. Verily, the Messenger of Allah was given the knowledge of what has been and what is to come until the Day of Resurrection, and we have inherited it from the Messenger of Allah as an inheritance."
65.book: Tafsir Ahl al-Bayt (peace be upon them), Vol. 8, p. 544

65.ar: الرّسول (- عَنْ أَبِی أُمَامَةَ: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ (قَالَ ذَاتَ یَوْمٍ لِأَصْحَابِهِ: أَ لَا أُحَدِّثُکُمْ عَنِ الخِضْر؟ قَالُوا: بَلَی یَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ (قَالَ: بَیْنَا هُوَ یَمْشِی فِی سُوقٍ مِنْ أَسْوَاقِ بَنِی إِسْرَائِیلَ إِذْ بَصُرَ بِهِ مِسْکِینٌ، فَقَالَ: تَصَدَّقْ عَلَیَّ بَارَکَ اللَّهُ فِیکَ. قَالَ الخِضْر: آمَنْتُ بِاللَّهِ مَا یَقْضِی اللَّهُ یَکُونُ مَا عِنْدِی مِنْ شَیْءٍ أُعْطِیکَهُ. قَالَ الْمِسْکِینُ: بِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ لَمَّا تَصَدَّقْتَ عَلَیَّ إِنِّی رَأَیْتُ الْخَیْرَ فِی وَجْهِکَ وَ رَجَوْتُ الْخَیْرَ عِنْدَکَ. قَالَ الخِضْر: آمَنْتُ بِاللَّهِ إِنَّکَ سَأَلْتَنِی بِأَمْرٍ عَظِیمٍ مَا عِنْدِی مِنْ شَیْءٍ أُعْطِیکَهُ إِلَّا أَنْ تَأْخُذَنِی فَتَبِیعَنِی. قَالَ الْمِسْکِینُ: وَ هَلْ یَسْتَقِیمُ هَذَا؟ قَالَ: الْحَقَّ أَقُولُ لَکَ إِنَّکَ سَأَلْتَنِی بِأَمْرٍ عَظِیمٍ سَأَلْتَنِی بِوَجْهِ رَبِّی عَزَّوَجَلَّ، أَمَا إِنِّی لَا أُخَیِّبُکَ فِی مَسْأَلَتِی بِوَجْهِ رَبِّی فَبِعْنِی فَقَدَّمَهُ إِلَی السُّوقِ فَبَاعَهُ بِأَرْبَعِمِائَةِ دِرْهَمٍ فَمَکَثَ عِنْدَ الْمُشْتَرِی زَمَاناً لَا یَسْتَعْمِلُهُ فِی شَیْءٍ. فَقَالَ الخِضْر (: إِنَّمَا ابْتَعْتَنِی الْتِمَاسَ خِدْمَتِی فَمُرْنِی بِعَمَلٍ. قَالَ: إِنِّی أَکْرَهُ أَنْ أَشُقَّ عَلَیْکَ إِنَّکَ شَیْخٌ کَبِیرٌ. قَالَ: لَسْتَ تَشُقُّ عَلَیَّ. قَالَ: فَقُمْ فَانْقُلْ هَذِهِ الْحِجَارَةَ. قَالَ: وَ کَانَ لَا یَنْقُلُهَا دُونَ سِتَّةِ نَفَرٍ فِی یَوْمٍ. فَقَامَ فَنَقَلَ الْحِجَارَةَ فِی سَاعَتِهِ فَقَالَ لَهُ: أَحْسَنْتَ وَ أَجْمَلْتَ وَ أَطَقْتَ مَا لَمْ یُطِقْهُ أَحَدٌ. قَالَ: ثُمَّ عَرَضَ لِلرَّجُلِ سَفَرٌ فَقَالَ: إِنِّی أَحْسَبُکَ أَمِیناً فَاخْلُفْنِی فِی أَهْلِی خِلَافَةً حَسَنَةً وَ إِنِّی أَکْرَهُ أَنْ أَشُقَّ عَلَیْکَ. قَالَ: لَسْتَ تَشُقُّ عَلَیَّ. قَالَ: فَاضْرِبْ مِنَ اللَّبِنِ شَیْئاً حَتَّی أَرْجِعَ إِلَیْکَ قَالَ فَخَرَجَ الرَّجُلُ لِسَفَرِهِ وَ رَجَعَ وَ قَدْ شَیَّدَ بِنَاءَهُ فَقَالَ لَهُ الرَّجُلُ أَسْأَلُکَ بِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ مَا حَسَبُکَ وَ مَا أَمْرُکَ. قَالَ: إِنَّکَ سَأَلْتَنِی بِأَمْرٍ عَظِیمٍ بِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ عَزَّوَجَلَّ وَ وَجْهُ اللَّهِ عَزَّوَجَلَّ أَوْقَعَنِی فِی الْعُبُودِیَّةِ وَ سَأُخْبِرُکَ مَنْ أَنَا؟ أَنَا الخِضْر الَّذِی سَمِعْتَ بِهِ، سَأَلَنِی مِسْکِینٌ صَدَقَةً وَ لَمْ یَکُنْ عِنْدِی شَیْءٌ أُعْطِیهِ فَسَأَلَنِی بِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ عَزَّوَجَلَّ فَأَمْکَنْتُهُ مِنْ رَقَبَتِی فَبَاعَنِی فَأُخْبِرُکَ أَنَّهُ مَنْ سُئِلَ بِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ عَزَّوَجَلَّ فَرَدَّ سَائِلَهُ وَ هُوَ قَادِرٌ عَلَی ذَلِکَ وَقَفَ یَوْمَ الْقِیَامَةِ لَیْسَ لِوَجْهِهِ جِلْدٌ وَ لَا لَحْمٌ وَ لَا دَمٌ إِلَّا عَظْمٌ یَتَقَعْقَعُ. قَالَ الرَّجُلُ: شَقَقْتُ عَلَیْکَ وَ لَمْ أَعْرِفْکَ. قَالَ: لَا بَأْسَ أَبْقَیْتَ وَ أَحْسَنْتَ قَالَ بِأَبِی أَنْتَ وَ أُمِّی احْکُمْ فِی أَهْلِی وَ مَالِی بِمَا أَرَاکَ اللَّهُ عَزَّوَجَلَّ أَمْ أُخَیِّرُکَ فَأُخَلِّی سَبِیلَکَ. قَالَ: أَحَبُّ إِلَیَّ أَنْ تُخَلِّیَ سَبِیلِی فَأَعْبُدَ اللَّهَ عَلَی سَبِیلِهِ.
65.fa: از ابوامامه روایت است: رسول خدا (صلی الله علیه و آله) روزی به اصحابش فرمود: «آیا می‌خواهید در مورد خضر (علیه السلام) برایتان داستانی بگویم»؟ گفتند: «بله»، فرمود: «روزی در یکی از بازارهای بنی اسرائیل راه می‌رفت که یک مسکینی او را دید و گفت: «خداوند به تو برکت دهد، چیزی به من صدقه بده». خضر (علیه السلام) گفت: «به خدا ایمان آوردم که هرچه او بخواهد انجام می‌شود چیزی ندارم که به تو ببخشم». مسکین گفت: «به خدا سوگنت میدهم که صدقهای به من بدهی، من خیر و برکت را در چهرهات دیدم و امید خیر از تو دارم». خضر (علیه السلام) گفت: «به خدا ایمان آوردم که تو به امری عظیم چیزی از من خواستی و من چیزی ندارم که به تو ببخشم جز اینکه من را ببری و در بازار بفروشی». آن مرد فقیر گفت: «و آیا این کار امکان دارد و درست است»؟ خضر (علیه السلام) گفت: «راست می‌گویم چون به امری عظیم چیزی از من خواستی. تو من را به خداوند عزّوجلّ قسم دادی و چون به امری عظیم چیزی از من خواستی، من نمیخواهم تو را ناامید کنم پس من را ببر و بفروش»، پس آن مرد خضر (علیه السلام) را به بازار برد و به چهار صد درهم فروخت و خضر (علیه السلام) زمانی در نزد صاحبش ماند و کاری را به او نمی‌داد که انجام دهد. خضر (علیه السلام) گفت: «تو به خاطر این من را خریدی که برایت کار بکنم پس به من دستور بده تا کاری را برایت انجام بدهم». آن مرد گفت: «من دوست ندارم که بر تو سخت بگیرم چون تو پیر هستی». خضر گفت: «نه تو بر من سخت نمیگیری - چنین تصور مکن -». آن مرد گفت: «پس برو و آن سنگ را جابجا کن». - که آن سنگ را فقط شش نفر در یک روز کامل می‌توانستند حمل بکنند -. پس خضر (علیه السلام) آن سنگ را به تنهایی در طول یک ساعت حمل کرد. آن مرد به او گفت: «آفرین تو کاری را انجام دادی که هیچ‌کس نمی‌توانست آن را انجام دهد». سپس آن مرد به سفری تجاری رفت و به خضر گفت: «من تو را امین خودم می‌دانم پس در نزد خانوادهام جانشین من باش و با آنها درست رفتار کن، و من نمی‌خواهم بر تو سخت بگیرم». خضر گفت «نه بر من سخت نیست بگو چکاری بکنم»؟ گفت: «تا من بر می‌گردم مقداری خشت بزن». پس آن مرد به سفرش رفت و کارش را انجام داد و برگشت و دید که ساختمانش ساخته شده است. به خضر (علیه السلام) گفت: «تو را قسم می‌دهم که تو چه کسی هستی؟ و داستان تو چیست»؟ خضر گفت: «تو به امری عظیم مرا قسم دادی یعنی به خداوند متعال و قسم به خداوند متعال مرا در بردگی انداخت. اکنون به تو خبر میدهم که کیستم. من خضر هستم که نامم را شنیدی؛ مرد فقیری از من چیزی درخواست کرد و من هم چیزی نداشتم که به او ببخشم پس من را به خدا قسم داد که به او چیزی بدهم من هم خودم را به او دادم که من را بفروشد و او نیز من را فروخت. پس بدان هرکس با خداوند از او چیزی بخواهند، ولی او چیزی نبخشد درحالی‌که بتواند چیزی ببخشد در روز قیامت، صورتش پوست و گوشت و خون ندارد و فقط استخوان هایی هستنند که تکان می‌خورند». آن مرد گفت: «بر تو سخت گرفتم و نمی‌دانستم که چه کسی هستی». گفت: «مشکلی ندارد تو بر من رحم کردی و با من خوب رفتار کردی». و به خضر گفت: «فدایت بشوم آن طور که خداوند عزّوجلّ به تو نشان داده است در مورد من و خانواده و مالم دستور بده یا این-که تو را مخ-یر میگردانم پ-س تو را آزاد کن-م»؟ خضر (علیه السلام) گفت: «من دوست دارم که تو من را آزاد کنی تا خداوند را عبادت کنم. سپاس برای خداوندی که من را در دام بندگی انداخت سپس من را از آن نجات داد».
65.en: It is narrated from Abu Umamah that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said one day to his companions: "Shall I tell you about al-Khidr?" They replied: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "While he was walking in one of the markets of the Children of Israel, a poor man saw him and said: 'May Allah bless you, give me charity.' Al-Khidr said: 'I believe in Allah; whatever Allah decrees will come to pass, but I have nothing to give you.' The poor man said: 'I adjure you by the Face of Allah to give me charity, for I have seen goodness in your face and I hope for goodness from you.' Al-Khidr said: 'I believe in Allah; you have asked me by a great matter. I have nothing to give you except that you take me and sell me.' The poor man said: 'Is this appropriate?' He replied: 'I tell you the truth, you have asked me by a great matter; you have asked me by the Face of my Lord, the Almighty and Majestic. I will not disappoint you in your request by the Face of my Lord, so sell me.' He took him to the market and sold him for four hundred dirhams. He remained with the buyer for a time, and the buyer did not assign him any work. Al-Khidr said: 'You bought me to serve you, so command me to do some work.' The man said: 'I dislike burdening you, for you are an old man.' He replied: 'You will not be burdening me.' The man said: 'Then stand up and move these stones.' (It was said that these stones could not be moved by fewer than six men in a day). He stood up and moved the stones in an hour. The man said to him: 'You have done well and beautifully, and you have accomplished what no one else could.' Then the man had to go on a journey and said: 'I consider you trustworthy, so be my deputy over my family in a good manner, and I dislike burdening you.' He replied: 'You will not be burdening me.' The man said: 'Then make some bricks until I return to you.' The man went on his journey, and when he returned, he found that he had finished the construction. The man said to him: 'I ask you by the Face of Allah, who are you and what is your affair?' He replied: 'You have asked me by a great matter, by the Face of Allah, the Almighty and Majestic, and the Face of Allah has brought me into servitude. I will tell you who I am: I am al-Khidr, whom you have heard of. A poor man asked me for charity, and I had nothing to give him, so he asked me by the Face of Allah, the Almighty and Majestic, and I surrendered myself to him, so he sold me. I inform you that whoever is asked by the Face of Allah, the Almighty and Majestic, and refuses the requester while he is able to do so, will stand on the Day of Resurrection with no skin, flesh, or blood on his face, only rattling bones.' The man said: 'I have burdened you, and I did not know who you were.' He replied: 'There is no harm; you have been kind and have done well.' The man said: 'May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, judge regarding my family and my wealth as Allah, the Almighty and Majestic, shows you, or I will give you the choice and set you free.'
